# Hive Mind REA - portable stack definition
#
# This file is the single source of truth for what the stack contains.
# Installers read it; nothing in here is OS-specific. Per-platform paths are
# derived at install time by scripts/bootstrap.py, never hard-coded.
#
# Schema: stack/v1

schema: stack/v1
name: hive-mind-rea
version: 4.0.0
description: >
  Local-first AI development and reverse-engineering suite.
  Runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and inside WSL. Degrades gracefully:
  every component is optional except the runtime itself.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runtime requirements. Used by scripts/doctor.py to score the machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
requirements:
  python: ">=3.10"
  ram_gb_min: 8
  ram_gb_recommended: 16
  disk_gb_min: 20
  disk_gb_recommended: 60
  cpu_cores_min: 2

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ports. Chosen to avoid common conflicts; each can be overridden by env var
# of the same name in the `env` key.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ports:
  ollama: 11434
  grafana: 3000
  lmstudio: 1234
  openclaw: 18789

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Components. `detect` is a command that proves the component works.
# `

udio: 1234
  openclaw: 18789

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Components. `detect` is a command that proves the component works.
# `install` lists the per-platform package-manager commands.
# `required: false` means the stack still runs without it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
components:

  - id: ollama
    label: Ollama
    required: true
    role: Local LLM runtime
    detect: { command: ["ollama", "--version"] }
    env: { OLLAMA_HOST: "127.0.0.1:11434" }
    install:
      windows: ["winget install --id Ollama.Ollama -e"]
      macos:   ["brew install ollama"]
      linux:   ["curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh"]
    models:
      # Chosen for 8 GB RAM / CPU-only. Pull in this order; stop when RAM is tight.
      - { name: "lfm3:1.7b",          size_gb: 1.1, note: "fast default, tool calling" }
      - { name: "qwen2.5-coder:1.5b", size_gb: 1.0, note: "best small coding model" }
      - { name: "llama3.2:3b",        size_gb: 2.0, note: "general reasoning" }
      - { name: "qwen3:4b",           size_gb: 2.6, note: "upper bound for 8 GB" }

  - id: hermes
    label: Hermes
    required: false
    role: Supervisor agent, routes and delegates
    detect: { command: ["hermes", "--version"] }
    env: { HERMES_HOME: "${DATA_DIR}/hermes" }

  - id: opencode
    label: Open

e
    role: Supervisor agent, routes and delegates
    detect: { command: ["hermes", "--version"] }
    env: { HERMES_HOME: "${DATA_DIR}/hermes" }

  - id: opencode
    label: OpenCode
    required: false
    role: Coding agent with subagent delegation
    detect: { command: ["opencode", "--version"] }
    install:
      windows: ["npm install -g opencode-ai"]
      macos:   ["npm install -g opencode-ai", "brew install opencode"]
      linux:   ["npm install -g opencode-ai", "curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash"]

  - id: craft-anything
    label: Craft Anything
    required: false
    role: Software investigation MCP server
    detect:
      command: ["craft-anything-cli", "--version"]
      # Fallback probe: a correct MCP server answers initialize in one line of JSON.
      mcp_probe: true
    install:
      windows: ["winget install --id CraftAnything.CraftAnything -e"]
      macos:   ["brew install --cask craft-anything"]
      linux:   ["curl -fsSL https://craftanything.dev/install.sh | sh"]

  - id: git
    label: Git
    required: true
    role: version control
    detect: { command: ["git", "--version"] }
    install:
      windows: ["winget install --id Git.Git -e"]
      macos:   ["xcode-select --install", "brew install git"]
      linux:   ["sudo apt-get install -y git"]

  - id: node
    label: Node.js
    required: false
    role: runs MCP servers, OpenCo

"xcode-select --install", "brew install git"]
      linux:   ["sudo apt-get install -y git"]

  - id: node
    label: Node.js
    required: false
    role: runs MCP servers, OpenCode
    detect: { command: ["node", "--version"] }
    install:
      windows: ["winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e"]
      macos:   ["brew install node"]
      linux:   ["sudo apt-get install -y nodejs npm"]

  - id: grafana
    label: Grafana
    required: false
    role: dashboards over the Obsidian work matrix
    detect: { http: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health" }
    install:
      windows: ["winget install --id GrafanaLabs.Grafana.OSS -e"]
      macos:   ["brew install grafana"]
      linux:   ["sudo apt-get install -y grafana"]

  - id: docker
    label: Docker
    required: false
    role: optional heavy services
    detect: { command: ["docker", "version", "--format", "{{.Server.Version}}"] }
    install:
      windows: ["winget install --id Docker.DockerDesktop -e"]
      macos:   ["brew install --cask docker"]
      linux:   ["sudo apt-get install -y docker.io"]

# ${VARS} are substituted by scripts/bootstrap.py.

mcp_servers:

  - id: craft-anything
    transport: stdio
    command: ["${CRAFT_ANYTHING_CLI}", "mcp"]
    note: >
      Investigation memory lives in the project directory. Always run it with

    enabled: true

  - id: filesystem

    enabled: true

  - id: git
    transport: stdio
    command: ["uvx", "mcp-server-git", "--repository", "${WORKSPACE}"]
    enabled: false

  - id: fetch
    transport: stdio
    command: ["uvx", "mcp-server-fetch"]
    enabled: false

chunks.heading: Knowledge base
chunks.text:
# Knowledge base

A portable, offline index of everything in this repository plus the build facts
for the laptop/desktop. Pull the repo, run one command, and any agent can search
it without network access.

chunks.heading: Files
chunks.text:
## Files

| File | What it is | Commit it? |
|---|---|---|
| `data/build-facts.json` | Curated, verified machine/toolchain/MCP facts | Yes — edit by hand |
| `data/index.json` | Generated structured dump (documents, headings, links, facts) | Yes — diffable |
| `data/knowledge.db` | Generated SQLite + FTS5 database | Yes — ~0.9 MB |
| `scripts/build_index.py` | Rebuilds both generated files | Yes |
| `scripts/query.py` | CLI search/read | Yes |

The database is committed on purpose: the desktop should not need Python to
read the data. Anything that can open SQLite (DB Browser, DBeaver, Datasette,
Python, Node, Go) can read it.

chunks.heading: Rebuild after editing docs
chunks.text:
## Rebuild after editing docs

```bash
python scripts/build_index.py
```

Safe to run repeatedly. It excludes `repos/`, `.git`, `node_modules`, Hermes
caches/logs/sessions and every `*.db`, so only publishable text is indexed.

chunks.heading: Query
chunks.text:
## Query

```bash
python scripts/query.py --stats
python scripts/query.py --search "bios ram"
python scripts/query.py --search "mcp hermes" --limit 5
python scripts/query.py --facts machine
python scripts/query.py --facts mcp
python scripts/query.py --facts toolchain
python scripts/query.py --docs
python scripts/query.py --doc docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md
```

From another language, open `data/knowledge.db` directly:

```sql
-- full-text search with context
SELECT path, heading, snippet(chunks_fts, 0, '«', '»', '…', 14)
FROM chunks_fts
WHERE chunks_fts MATCH '"mcp" AND "hermes"'
ORDER BY bm25(chunks_fts)
LIMIT 10;

-- every verified fact about the machine
SELECT key, value FROM facts WHERE category = 'machine';

-- pending work
SELECT key, value FROM facts WHERE category = 'pending';

-- documents and headings
SELECT d.path, h.level, h.text, h.line
FROM headings h JOIN documents d ON d.id = h.doc_id
WHERE d.path LIKE 'docs/%'
ORDER BY d.path, h.line;
```

chunks.heading: Schema
chunks.text:
## Schema

```
documents(id, path, kind, title, modified, sha256, words)
headings(id, doc_id, level, text, line)
chunks(id, doc_id, heading, line_start, text)
links(id, doc_id, target)
facts(id, category, key, value)
chunks_fts(text, heading, path UNINDEXED, doc_id UNINDEXED)  -- FTS5, porter
```

`facts.category` is one of: `machine`, `windows_tuning`, `toolchain`, `agents`,
`mcp`, `projects`, `lessons`, `pending`, `component`, `stack`.

chunks.heading: Describing a new machine
chunks.text:
## Describing a new machine

The facts are not laptop-specific by design. On a new desktop:

1. Copy `data/build-facts.json` and update `machine`, `toolchain`, `projects`.
2. Run `python scripts/build_index.py`.
3. Commit. The old values stay in git history if you need to compare.

Do not put secrets, tokens, session transcripts or `repos/` contents in this
folder. The index is meant to be public-safe.

chunks.heading: Agent actions: what is allowed, what needs a human
chunks.text:
# Agent actions: what is allowed, what needs a human

This file is the contract between the human and **any** agent working in this
repository — OpenCode, Hermes, Claude, Codex, a local model, or something not
written yet. Read it before acting.

The rule is simple: **reading is free, writing is cheap, spending is not.**

---

chunks.heading: Tier 0 — do it without asking
chunks.text:
## Tier 0 — do it without asking

| Action | Notes |
|---|---|
| Read files, logs, configs, databases | Never modify what you read |
| Run `scripts/doctor.py` | Read-only health check |
| Search the web, fetch pages | `scripts/research.py` |
| Take browser snapshots, screenshots | Evidence gathering |
| Inspect processes, services, memory, disk | Read-only host queries |
| Write scratch files to the OS temp directory | Use `%TEMP%` / `$TMPDIR` / `/tmp` |

chunks.heading: Tier 1 — do it, then say what you did
chunks.text:
## Tier 1 — do it, then say what you did

| Action | Notes |
|---|---|
| Write files inside this repository | Follow existing layout and style |
| Install a **user-scope** package: `pip install --user`, `npm i -g`, `uv tool install` | Never system-wide without Tier 2 |
| Create or edit a note in the Obsidian vault | Append, do not overwrite history |
| Generate reports, charts, diagrams, Office documents | `scripts/office.py`, `scripts/viz.py` |
| Fill a form field, select an option, tick a checkbox in a browser | Reversible; do not submit |
| Change a service from Automatic to Manual | Reversible with one command |
| Write to `HKCU` / a user dotfile | User-scope only |

chunks.heading: Tier 2 — ask first, every time
chunks.text:
## Tier 2 — ask first, every time

| Action | Why |
|---|---|
| **Buy anything** | Money leaves the account |
| **Sell anything** | Money and third parties |
| Place a bid, book travel, reserve stock | Creates a commitment |
| Submit a payment, order or booking form | Irreversible |
| Enter card, bank or government ID details | Never do this without an explicit, in-conversation instruction naming the site |
| Send email, message or post publicly | Cannot be unsent |
| Delete files outside this repo | Could destroy the human's work |
| Install anything system-wide / with elevation | Affects the whole machine |
| Change BIOS, firmware or partition tables | Brick risk |
| Rotate, revoke or create credentials | Can lock the human out |

chunks.heading: The purchase protocol
chunks.text:
### The purchase protocol

Before any transaction, print and wait for explicit confirmation:

```
ABOUT TO BUY
  Item     : <exact product name and model number>
  Seller   : <site and seller account>
  Price    : <item price> + <shipping> = <total>
  Delivery : <address summary, last line only>
  Payment  : <card brand and last 4 digits — never the full number>
  Returns  : <window and conditions>
Confirm? Reply "yes" to continue.
```

Rules:

1. **One confirmation, one purchase.** A "yes" covers that item at that price
   only. Never reuse it for a second cart, a second item, or a re-price.
2. **Checkout stops at the final button.** Fill the basket, then hand control
   back. The human clicks "Pay".
3. **If the price changes** at any step, stop and re-confirm.
4. **Never store credentials.** No card numbers in files, configs, notes or
   commit history. If you find one, report it — do not use it.
5. **Never defeat a paywall, CAPTCHA, or verification step.**

chunks.heading: The sale protocol
chunks.text:
### The sale protocol

Selling additionally requires: the human owns the item, the listing text is
shown before publishing, and the price floor is stated in the conversation.
Publishing a listing counts as "post publicly" — Tier 2.

---

chunks.heading: Installing software
chunks.text:
## Installing software

Prefer the least invasive route that works, in this order:

1. **Already present?** Check `scripts/doctor.py` before installing anything.
2. **Project-local**: `pip install --target ./.venv`, `npm i --no-save`
3. **User-scope**: `pip install --user`, `npm i -g`, `uv tool install`
4. **System-wide**: ask first (Tier 2)

Platform commands:

| Task | Windows | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python packages | `python -m pip install --user X` | `python3 -m pip install --user X` | `python3 -m pip install --user X` |
| Global CLI | `npm i -g X` | `npm i -g X` | `npm i -g X` (or use `nvm`) |
| Package manager | `winget install X` | `brew install X` | `apt/dnf/pacman install X` |
| Elevation | UAC prompt, user clicks | `sudo`, user types password | `sudo` |

**Never** invent an administrator password, and never try to bypass UAC, `sudo`
or a password prompt. If elevation is needed, prepare the exact command, show
it, and let the human run it.

chunks.heading: Reporting dependencies
chunks.text:
### Reporting dependencies

If a script needs a package that is missing, say so in this shape:

```
Missing  : openpyxl
Needed by: scripts/office.py --to xlsx
Install  : python -m pip install --user openpyxl
Fallback : --to csv works without it
```

Always check whether a fallback exists before asking the human to install.

---

chunks.heading: Producing output
chunks.text:
## Producing output

| Want | Command | Opens in |
|---|---|---|
| Spreadsheet | `office.py --to xlsx out.xlsx` | Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc |
| Document | `office.py --to docx out.docx` | Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice Writer |
| Slides | `office.py --to pptx out.pptx` | PowerPoint, Google Slides, LibreOffice Impress |
| Plain table | `office.py --to csv out.csv` | Everything, including Google Sheets |
| Chart | `viz.py --chart bar ... -o out.svg` | Browsers, Word, PowerPoint, Google Slides |
| Diagram | `viz.py --mermaid flowchart ...` | GitHub, GitLab, Obsidian, the Review pane |
| Web page | `viz.py ... --html` | Any browser |

`.docx`, `.xlsx` and `.pptx` are ZIP-based Open XML. Google Drive converts them
on upload, so the same file serves both Microsoft and Google workspaces. When
the human needs a native Google file, upload the Microsoft one and let Drive
convert, or hand over the `.csv` for Sheets.

---

chunks.heading: Housekeeping
chunks.text:
## Housekeeping

- Leave the machine measurably better than you found it: report bytes freed,
  services changed, and what you did **not** do.
- Never claim a step succeeded without a command output that shows it.
- If something is not installed and cannot be found, say **"it does not exist
  on this machine"** rather than assuming it is broken.
- Keep notes in the vault and commit code; a fix that exists only in a chat
  log is lost.

chunks.heading: Claude Code deep dive — capabilities, free equivalents, what to adopt
chunks.text:
# Claude Code deep dive — capabilities, free equivalents, what to adopt

Research date: 2026-11-23. Primary sources: `code.claude.com/docs` (official),
`agentskills.io`, and the GitHub REST API for repository/licence facts.
Web search was unavailable (HTTP 402); all findings below came from direct fetches.

chunks.heading: 1. What Claude Code actually has now
chunks.text: ## 1. What Claude Code actually has now

chunks.heading: Core engine
chunks.text:
### Core engine
- Terminal CLI, IDE extensions (VS Code/Cursor/JetBrains), Desktop app and Web.
- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` memory files plus **auto memory** that saves learnings
  across sessions without the user writing anything.
- Git-native workflow: stages changes, writes commits, branches and opens PRs.
- Composable CLI: `claude -p "..."`, pipes, CI, `--agents`, `--append-subagent-system-prompt`.
- Scheduling: cloud routines, desktop scheduled tasks, `/loop`.
- Remote Control, Dispatch, `claude --teleport`, Slack `@Claude`, Chrome debugging.

chunks.heading: Skills (the biggest portable idea)
chunks.text:
### Skills (the biggest portable idea)
`SKILL.md` = YAML frontmatter + Markdown instructions, directory name is the
command. Skills follow the **Agent Skills open standard** (`agentskills.io`),
so they work across tools. Key frontmatter fields:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `name`, `description`, `when_to_use` | discovery and auto-invocation |
| `context: fork`, `agent`, `background` | run in a subagent context |
| `allowed-tools`, `disallowed-tools` | permission scoping |
| `model`, `effort` | per-skill model/effort override |
| `paths` | activate only for matching files |
| `hooks` | lifecycle hooks registered while the skill is active |
| `!`command`` | dynamic context injection (runs shell before Claude sees the skill) |
| `metadata`, `license` | open-standard extension fields |

Locations: managed settings → `~/.claude/skills/` → project `.claude/skills/` →
nested → plugin → claude.ai sync. Bundled skills include `/doctor`, `/code-review`,
`/batch`, `/debug`, `/loop`, `/run`, `/verify`, `/run-skill-generator`, `/claude-api`.
`/run` + `/verify` + a recorded `run-<name>` skill let a project follow a saved
launch/verify recipe instead of rediscovering it.

chunks.heading: Subagents
chunks.text:
### Subagents
Markdown files with `name`, `description`, `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`,
`permissionMode`, `mcpServers`, `hooks`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `memory`, `effort`,
`isolation: worktree`, `color`. Built-ins: Explore (read-only), Plan (read-only),
General-purpose, `claude`, statusline-setup, claude-code-guide, web-fetch.
They preserve context, enforce tool restrictions, route to cheaper models and
can run in isolated git worktrees.

chunks.heading: Hooks
chunks.text:
### Hooks
40+ lifecycle events: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`,
`PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `SubagentStart/Stop`,
`TaskCreated/Completed`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `TeammateIdle`, `PreCompact`,
`SessionEnd`, `FileChanged`, `ConfigChange`, `Elicitation`, and more.
Handlers can be `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt` or `agent`; they can deny
or rewrite tool calls, and `PostToolUse` can auto-format or lint after edits.

chunks.heading: Agent teams (experimental)
chunks.text:
### Agent teams (experimental)
`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`. A lead session spawns teammates that
have **separate contexts**, a **shared task list** and a **mailbox**
(`~/.claude/teams/{team}/inboxes/{agent}.json`). Teammates self-claim unblocked
tasks, message each other directly, and can be individually steered. Quality
gates use `TeammateIdle` / `TaskCompleted` hooks (exit 2 = keep working).
This is the closest official analogue to the team the user asked for.

chunks.heading: Dynamic workflows
chunks.text:
### Dynamic workflows
A JavaScript script (`agent()`, `pipeline()`, `parallel()`, `phase()`)
orchestrates dozens-to-hundreds of subagents in the background. Plans live in
code, not in the model's context; runs are **resumable**, agents auto-retry on
stall (up to 6 attempts), and results can be cross-checked adversarially.
`/deep-research` is the bundled example; `ultracode` triggers automatic workflows.

chunks.heading: Safety / licensing boundary
chunks.text:
### Safety / licensing boundary
- MIT/Apache/CC0 projects are safe to **study and reuse patterns from**, with
  attribution and their licence retained. Do **not** paste their code into `app/`.
- Repos with **no licence** are not licensed for reuse. Treat them as reading material only.
- Decompiled/rebuilt Claude Code binaries may breach the Anthropic terms of
  service and can carry malware or telemetry. **Do not install or run them.**
- We adopt **open standards and documented behaviour** (Agent Skills, MCP, hooks,
  subagent frontmatter, workflow shape), not proprietary source or keys.

chunks.heading: 3. Gap analysis: what this build is missing
chunks.text:
## 3. Gap analysis: what this build is missing

Already present: 13-phase REA loop, ten inter-agent languages, free-service
registry, human gate, checkpoint ledger, project knowledge databases,
multi-member auto-selection, message bus, task board, handoffs.

Missing (highest value first):

1. **Skills registry with `SKILL.md` shape** — no reusable, on-demand procedure
   packages; the team re-derives the same workflows every round.
2. **Hooks / lifecycle gates** — no automatic policy on tool use, task completion
   or stop; nothing prevents a bad write or a premature "done".
3. **Subagent definitions** — roles exist as names only; no tool restrictions,
   model routing, worktree isolation or max-turn limits.
4. **Workflow engine** — the loop is sequential; no `parallel()`/`pipeline()`
   fan-out, resume, or adversarial cross-check of findings.
5. **Agent teams semantics** — no explicit lead/teammate mailbox and shared task
   claim protocol with file-locking-style safety.
6. **Auto memory + `/doctor`** — no cross-session learnings or self-checkup that
   reports and fixes setup problems.
7. **Recorded run/verify recipe** — builds succeed but the launch/check recipe is
   not saved as a reusable skill.

chunks.heading: 4. Concrete adoption plan (implemented in `app/`)
chunks.text:
## 4. Concrete adoption plan (implemented in `app/`)

Add data-driven registries to `app/src/studio.js`, exposed in the UI:

- `SKILLS`: built-ins `doctor`, `verify`, `run`, `deep-research`, `code-review`,
  `reverse-api`, `taste-skill`, plus a project `run-<name>` recipe. Fields mirror
  Agent Skills: `name`, `description`, `when_to_use`, `context`, `allowedTools`,
  `model`, `paths`, `hooks`.
- `HOOKS`: events `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `TaskCompleted`, `Stop`,
  `SubagentStop`, `TeammateIdle`; handler types `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`,
  `prompt`, `agent`; decisions allow/deny/rewrite with a reason.
- `SUBAGENT_TYPES`: `Explore` (read-only), `Plan` (read-only), `General-purpose`,
  `web-fetch`, each with `tools`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`,
  `isolation: worktree`.
- `WORKFLOWS`: script-shaped phases with `agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`,
  resume from saved results, stall retry and adversarial verification.
- `AGENT_TEAMS`: lead + teammates + shared task list + mailbox, self-claim and
  direct messaging, with `TeammateIdle`/`TaskCompleted` quality gates.
- `AUTO_MEMORY`: cross-session facts written to local state, surfaced in reports.
- `DOCTOR`: checks MCP wiring, provider/model health, free-service registry,
  broken links and build output; offers fixes.

chunks.heading: Additional concrete takeaways for this build
chunks.text:
### Additional concrete takeaways for this build

1. **Research-first development** (ECC): no implementation until evidence is
   gathered and cited. Our `discover`/`reverse` phases already do this; make the
   rule explicit in the phase body.
2. **Instincts** (ECC): persistent, small learned rules that survive sessions —
   different from facts in memory. Add an `INSTINCTS` registry that the team
   writes after a failed approach and reads before each phase.
3. **Subagent-driven development** (superpowers): decompose a task into
   independent subagent jobs with verification before merge. Our `WORKFLOWS`
   registry should require a verifier agent after each builder agent.
4. **Token efficiency with recoverable originals** (caveman): compress tool
   output in the channel but store the full original in the project database,
   with a pointer. This keeps the UI fast without losing evidence.
5. **Taste / art direction** (taste-skill): when reverse-engineering a visual
   target, capture not only tokens but the *rationale* (why 480px, why mono)
   and verify in a browser. Our `taste-skill` built-in should do this.
6. **Diagrams as code** (archify): use Mermaid for plans and architecture,
   already supported by `scripts/viz.py`.
7. **Catalogue discovery**: treat `awesome-llm-apps` and `awesome-reverse-engineer-anything`
   as append-only source lists, not dependencies.

chunks.heading: Concrete additions selected from the third wave
chunks.text:
### Concrete additions selected from the third wave

1. **Isolated per-member computer** (suparagent): each team member gets a
   namespaced workspace in the shared state, not just a role label.
2. **Routines** (suparagent): named recurring jobs per member, in addition to
   our global auto-mode interval.
3. **Access-control registry** (ryu) + **sandbox flag** (poco-claw, AstraBox):
   every tool call checks `AGENT_ACCESS` before running; risky actions are
   sandboxed or sent to the human gate.
4. **Run monitor** (ryu): a visible list of active/finished runs with owner,
   phase, cost/tokens and outcome, not just the activity log.
5. **Skill catalogue** (flowwink): `SKILLS` should be loaded from a catalogue
   with tags and counts, not a fixed list; add `CATALOGUES` for external lists.
6. **Durable agent memory + graph** (swarmvault): our per-project SQLite DB is
   the memory store; add a `graph` view exporting nodes/edges to Mermaid.
7. **Self-evolution ledger** (lemonai): record failed approaches as instincts.
8. **One-command bootstrap** (selfhost-ai): a `bootstrap-free-stack` skill that
   documents installing only free/self-hosted services.

Not adopted: anti-detect/stealth browser projects (`oss-invisible/dots`) —
evading bot protections is out of scope and conflicts with our human-oversight rule.

chunks.heading: 4d. Fourth wave — general reverse-engineering practice
chunks.text:
## 4d. Fourth wave — general reverse-engineering practice

Source: the CC0-licensed `AIshihzong/awesome-reverse-engineer-anything` list,
fetched directly (287 lines). Every entry is checked and tagged REA / AI-RE /
Rebuild / Claim?. Its own summary is that of six most-shared cases, only one
actually says it used REA.

chunks.heading: The most decision-relevant evidence
chunks.text:
### The most decision-relevant evidence

- `pablodiazjorge/rea-lab`: five preregistered studies, 482 Claude Code runs.
  **No significant solve-rate gain from REA**; REA runs took about twice the
  time and cost. Study 2: 11/24 solved without REA vs 4/24 with it (p = 0.092).
- `aicodeking/leanrea`: one **8 KB skill** that drives Ghidra/Hopper/JADX
  directly through the shell instead of an MCP layer. 36 runs: same accuracy,
  **38% less wall time, 35% less cost, 56% fewer turns, 60% fewer tokens**,
  and 34.5k tokens of context instead of 400.7k. Caveat: three reps per cell,
  one model, one machine, and the external tools were absent in both arms.
- Conclusion for us: **prefer lean skills + direct CLI tools over a large MCP
  layer**. Our use of the Craft Anything CLI rather than loading 300+ tools into
  context is already the right shape. Keep registries small and load on demand.

chunks.heading: Practical patterns worth adopting
chunks.text:
### Practical patterns worth adopting

1. **Hash-pinned evidence + differential tests** (`devtechedge/feature-heist`):
   every rebuild stores the evidence with a hash and has a differential test
   against the original. Our project DB already stores sha256 per source; add
   a differential check to `verify`.
2. **Behaviour recordings** (`erkamyaman/rust-anything`, `ruguevara/zx-reaper`,
   `AsyncFinn/rook`): record what the original returns/throws, rewrite one
   piece, replay the recording, then move on. This is stronger than visual
   similarity alone. Add a `BEHAVIOUR_RECORDINGS` ledger.
3. **Evidence IDs on every conclusion** (`pablodiazjorge/rea-casebook`): no
   finding without a cited `evidence_id`. Craft Anything already does this;
   require it in our report template.
4. **Sandbox + tool allowlist + hash-approved inputs** (`dagoSte/rea-safe-agents`,
   `lalbers/agent-sandbox`): no network, read-only roots, no capabilities, and
   only an allowlisted subset of tools. Maps directly onto our planned
   `AGENT_ACCESS` registry and human gate.
5. **Findings → spec → architecture → plan → validation**
   (`ShadowSwaps/REA-Reconstruction-Companion`): our `intake`/`plan` phases
   should emit these five artefacts explicitly.
6. **Clean-room default, deep mode opt-in** (Craft Anything itself): keep
   `clean_room: false` only in deep mode; never copy proprietary code.
7. **Leg

6. **Clean-room default, deep mode opt-in** (Craft Anything itself): keep
   `clean_room: false` only in deep mode; never copy proprietary code.
7. **Legal boundary** (the whole list): own-copy only, interoperability,

chunks.heading: Not adopted

# Hive Mind REA Template - Windows 10/11 Install Notes
Updated: 2026-11-10 (i3-1005G1, 7.75GB RAM)

chunks.heading: Core (already in this setup)
chunks.text:
## Core (already in this setup)
- Ollama: `winget install Ollama.Ollama` or installer; `ollama pull bonsai-2:4b lfm3:1.7b laya`
- Hermes: install Hermes Agent/Desktop; set `HERMES_HOME=%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`; copy `hermes/config.yaml` and `hermes/profiles/*`
- OpenCode: copy `opencode/agents/*.md` to `~/.config/opencode/agents/`
- Docker Desktop (WSL2): enable WSL, install Docker Desktop; engine 29.x verified. Start UI via `Docker Desktop.exe`
- Grafana: service on :3000; copy `grafana/provisioning/*` to Grafana conf/provisioning (Admin) and restart service
- Obsidian: open `obsidian-vault/` as vault

chunks.heading: MCP servers (configure in OpenCode/Claude/Hermes MCP config)
chunks.text:
## MCP servers (configure in OpenCode/Claude/Hermes MCP config)
Use `mcp/opencode-mcp.example.json` as template. Most run via `npx -y <pkg>` (Node 18+).
- **Playwright MCP**: `npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest` (Microsoft)
- **Chrome DevTools MCP**: `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` (or package per your client)
- **Perplexity MCP**: `npx -y server-perplexity-ask` + `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`
- **Firecrawl MCP**: `npx -y firecrawl-mcp` + `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`
- **Apify MCP**: `npx -y @apify/actors-mcp-server` + `APIFY_TOKEN`
- **Reference MCP servers**: `@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`, `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`, `uvx mcp-server-git`, `uvx mcp-server-fetch`
- **VidIQ / Skool / Higgsfield MCPs**: require vendor API keys or community packages - add endpoints/keys in `.env` once obtained

chunks.heading: Media / creator CLI (lightweight first)
chunks.text:
## Media / creator CLI (lightweight first)
- **FFmpeg**: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` (or `choco install ffmpeg`) - verify `ffmpeg -version`
- **yt-dlp**: `python -m pip install -U yt-dlp` or `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp`
- **Whisper**: prefer `pip install faster-whisper` (lighter) or `openai-whisper` (heavier, needs torch). On 7.75GB RAM use small/base models only.
- **Remotion**: `npx create-video@latest` in a project folder (Node 18+); render costs CPU/RAM
- **LiveKit**: `docker run --rm -p 7880:7880 -p 7881:7881 -p 7882:7882/udp livekit/livekit-server --dev` or see `docker/docker-compose.services.yml`; SDKs via npm/pip

chunks.heading: APIs (keys/OAuth required - do not commit)
chunks.text:
## APIs (keys/OAuth required - do not commit)
- **YouTube Analytics API**: Google Cloud project, enable YouTube Analytics/Data APIs, OAuth consent/credentials
- **Instagram API**: Meta Developer app, Instagram Graph API permissions/tokens
- Store in local `.env` or OS credential store

chunks.heading: Repos / apps requested (clone/configure selectively)
chunks.text:
## Repos / apps requested (clone/configure selectively)
- **OpenProject / Chatwoot / Cal.com**: self-host via Docker compose (see `docker/docker-compose.services.yml`) - heavy for 7.75GB RAM, run one at a time
- **Weknora, OpenWhispr, Cap, Open Higgsfield, VoiceStudio, OpenSEO, BaseMode**: identify official repos/releases and clone under `repos/` or install binaries; document in `docs/INTEGRATIONS.md`
- **aireceptionist, J.A.R.V.I.S, Grok bot clone, Scion, Mononoke**: clone exact GitHub repos once URLs confirmed (ambiguous names - verify before cloning)
- **claude x jev skill**: obtain skill package/source and place in Hermes/OpenCode skills path

chunks.heading: Performance tips (this machine)
chunks.text:
## Performance tips (this machine)
- Run **one** LLM server at a time (Ollama preferred). Keep Docker services minimal.
- Prefer `--disable-gpu` for Electron apps on Intel UHD if renderer crashes.
- `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=10m`; avoid loading >2GB models simultaneously.

chunks.heading: Craft Anything ↔ agents (MCP wiring)
chunks.text:
# Craft Anything ↔ agents (MCP wiring)

This is the fix for the failure that looks like **"the agent sits there for 15
minutes and nothing happens"**. It is almost never the MCP server. Check the
provider first.

chunks.heading: What actually happened (2026-11-23)
chunks.text:
## What actually happened (2026-11-23)

Craft Anything's builder was configured to use Hermes Agent. Records from
`build-activity.log` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\agent.log`:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 06:01:43 | Builder run starts |
| 06:12:09 | `custom didn't respond in time on any of 3 attempts` — the local provider at `127.0.0.1:11434` was **not running** |
| 06:12:17 | Hermes exits 2, `0 tokens in / 0 out` |
| 06:12:49 | Craft Anything retries automatically |
| 06:21:33 | `Gateway disconnected` — the run was killed while waiting |
| 06:29:19 | Retry again; a second 9,096-character session competes with the first |
| 06:33:24 | Same error; loop continues every ~90 s |

Two independent causes, both fixed:

1. **Provider down.** Ollama had been stopped to free RAM. Hermes' `model.provider:
   custom` points at `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`, so every call failed.
2. **Wrong model for an agent.** `bonsai-2:4b` has `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}` — no
   chat template. Measured: **57.7 s and ~200 hidden tokens to answer "OK"**, and
   empty content below 64 tokens. `laya` returns HTTP 400 on chat completions.

MCP itself was never broken: `hermes mcp test craft-anything` reports
**38 tools discovered**, and `hermes mcp list` shows it enabled.

chunks.heading: Use the preflight before every build
chunks.text:
## Use the preflight before every build

```powershell
# checks CLI, MCP handshake, OpenCode config, Hermes config, provider,
# and runs a real model smoke test
.\tools\agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider

# wiring only, no model call
.\tools\agent-preflight.ps1 -Quick

# machine-readable
.\tools\agent-preflight.ps1 -Json
```

Exit code `0` = safe to start the agent. `1` = at least one FAIL, with the exact
fix printed. A model that replies with empty content or takes > 60 s for "OK" is
flagged: long build prompts will be far worse.

chunks.heading: (Re)wire any agent
chunks.text:
## (Re)wire any agent

```powershell
.\tools\wire-craft-anything.ps1 -DryRun          # show changes
.\tools\wire-craft-anything.ps1 -Agent opencode,hermes
.\tools\wire-craft-anything.ps1 -Force           # replace an existing entry
```

The script is idempotent and writes a timestamped backup before editing
OpenCode's JSON. For agents it does not know, it prints the exact command.

chunks.text:
### Per-agent configuration

| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | `mcp.craft-anything = { type: "local", command: ["<cli>", "mcp"], enabled: true }` |
| Hermes | `hermes mcp add craft-anything --command "<cli>" --args mcp` | managed by `hermes mcp list/test` |

```

chunks.heading: Model policy: free cloud for builds
chunks.text:
## Model policy: free cloud for builds

The builder prompt is ~9,000 characters plus the system prompt and 38 tool
schemas. On an 8 GB CPU-only laptop, no local model can prefill and iterate
fast enough. **Use free cloud models; keep local models as fallback only.**

| Model | Where | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free` | Hermes via Nous API | tool call succeeded; 9k prompt answered in 2.6 s | **chosen for Hermes** |
| `opencode/hy4-flash-free` | OpenCode built-in | `opencode run` replied in 2.7 s, no credits needed | **chosen for OpenCode / Craft Anything** |
| `tencent/hy4-flash:free` | Nous free | no usable tool call | rejected |
| `upstage/solar-mini4:free` | Nous free | no tool call | rejected |
| `meituan/longcat-2.5:free` | Nous free | no tool call; 27 s on a long prompt | rejected |
| `qwen/qwen4-max:free` | Nous free | upstream capacity errors | rejected |
| any `...` paid model on Nous | Nous | HTTP 404: account has no credits | unavailable |
| `bonsai-2:4b` | local | 57.7 s for "OK", empty below 64 tokens, no chat template | **do not use as an agent** |
| `lfm3:1.7b` | local | "OK" in 15.8–20.8 s | fallback only |
| any 7B+ local | local | does not fit beside Chrome + WSL on 8 GB | desktop only |

Applied configuration:

```powershell
# Hermes - Nous free tier, tool-capable model
hermes config set model.default stepfun/step-3.7-flas

chunks.heading: Model policy: free cloud for builds
chunks.text:
ide Chrome + WSL on 8 GB | desktop only |

Applied configuration:

```powershell
# Hermes - Nous free tier, tool-capable model
hermes config set model.default stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free
hermes config set model.provider nous
hermes config set model.base_url https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1
hermes config set model.api_mode chat_completions
hermes config set auxiliary.coder.provider nous
hermes config set auxiliary.coder.model stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free
hermes config set auxiliary.group_router.provider nous
hermes config set auxiliary.group_router.model stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free
```

OpenCode uses `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:
`"model": "opencode/hy4-flash-free"` (MCP entries preserved).

Craft Anything's `craft.json` sets `"builder": "OpenCode"`, and CLI runs use
`--backend OpenCode`. Craft Anything's doctor reports all backends registered
and the MCP self-test healthy.

Nous access tokens are short-lived and Hermes refreshes them itself. Never copy
a token into the repo, an `opencode.json`, or an environment variable file.
Verify tool support before choosing any free model — most do not support it.

chunks.heading: Concurrency rule
chunks.text:
## Concurrency rule

Do **not** run two Hermes one-shots at the same time (Craft Anything's builder
plus a manual `hermes -z ...`, or two Craft Anything retries). They share one
gateway; the second one produces `Gateway disconnected; turn outcome is unknown`.
Craft Anything retries automatically every ~90 s, so a failed build can keep
colliding with itself.

Before starting a manual test, confirm no builder is running:

```powershell
Get-Process hermes -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

chunks.heading: Memory rule
chunks.text:
## Memory rule

Ollama is Tier 2: it is stopped at boot to save commit charge, and started on
demand. Hermes needs it. So the order is:

```powershell
.\tools\agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider   # starts Ollama and waits
# ... run the build ...
Stop-Process -Name 'ollama app','ollama' -Force   # reclaim ~3.6 GB when done
```

Never stop Ollama while a Craft Anything build is running.

chunks.heading: Failure signatures
chunks.text:
## Failure signatures

| Symptom | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `provider did not respond in time` | Ollama/API down or wrong URL | `agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider` |
| Empty model output, `finish=length` | model has no chat template / burns hidden tokens | switch model (see table) |
| `Gateway disconnected; turn outcome is unknown` | two Hermes runs collided, or the run was killed | run one at a time; resume the printed session |
| MCP tools missing in the agent | not registered, or wrong CLI path | `wire-craft-anything.ps1`, then `agent-preflight.ps1` |
| MCP `initialize` fails | CLI path wrong or package moved | pass `-Cli "<path>"`; test `craft-anything-cli.exe mcp --help` |
| 15 minutes of silence, 0 tokens | the above, compounded by retries | stop the loop, run preflight, then retry once |

chunks.heading: Verified state
chunks.text:
## Verified state

- Craft Anything CLI `0.6.0`
- MCP handshake: **38 tools**, stdio
- OpenCode: `mcp.craft-anything` enabled
- Hermes: `craft-anything` enabled
- Hermes model: `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free` @ Nous inference API (free tier)
- OpenCode model: `opencode/hy4-flash-free` (no credits required)
- Craft Anything builder: OpenCode (verified building the `polsia free v1` site)
- Preflight: all checks PASS; remote provider is reported as WARN (not probed)

chunks.heading: 2nd Brain (Obsidian Vault)
chunks.text:
## 2nd Brain (Obsidian Vault)

A "second brain" is a personal knowledge management (PKM) system — a digital repository for capturing, organizing, and retrieving information. Popularized by Tiago Forte's "Building a Second Brain" (BASB) methodology.

**You already have one.** Your Obsidian vault at `C:\Users\jpowe\Documents\ObsidianVault\` IS your second brain:

| BASB Concept | Your Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Capture** | Daily notes, agent vocabulary, project rows |
| **Organize** | Daily/, Work/, Projects/, Dashboards/, Templates/ |
| **Distill** | Agent_Vocabulary.md, Agent_Vocabulary_GrokBot.md |
| **Express** | Grafana dashboards, PROJECT_MATRIX.md, Daily logs |
| **PARA** (Projects/Areas/Resources/Archives) | Work/ (projects), Daily/ (areas), Agent_Vocabulary (resources), git history (archives) |

chunks.heading: Data Flow (every command is tracked)
chunks.text:
### Data Flow (every command is tracked)

```
User command (any tool)
    │
    ▼
Hermes Supervisor (@supervisor)
    │
    ├── Routes via laya /v1/systemone (is_coding, is_windows, is_risky)
    │
    ├── Delegates to worker (@coder, @windows, @researcher, etc.)
    │       │
    │       ├── Worker calls tool (Craft Anything, Ghidra, mitmproxy, etc.)
    │       │       │
    │       │       └── Tool result → Worker → Supervisor
    │       │
    │       └── Worker writes to Obsidian Daily (frontmatter: tokens_total, cost_usd, model_used, agent, grafana_dashboard)
    │
    ├── Supervisor writes to PROJECT_MATRIX.md (requestId dedup)
    │
    └── Grafana scrapes Prometheus (Ollama metrics) + Loki (log tails) + Obsidian frontmatter
            │
            └── Dashboard: /d/adw9qkn/work-tracking-matrix-e28094-hive-mind
```

chunks.heading: Craft Anything Integration
chunks.text:
### Craft Anything Integration

Craft Anything is connected as an **MCP server** to 9 agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, VS Code, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Hermes, Devin). When you run a Craft Anything command:

1. **Direct usage** (via `craft-anything-cli`): Results are stored in Craft Anything's own project files (`.cany` folders with evidence, memory, journal). These are NOT automatically pushed to Obsidian/Grafana.

2. **Via Hermes supervisor** (via MCP): When you send a command through Hermes (e.g., `@researcher investigate target.exe with Craft Anything`), the supervisor:
   - Routes the task via laya
   - Delegates to the appropriate worker
   - Worker calls Craft Anything MCP tools
   - Worker logs results to Obsidian Daily (frontmatter + notes)
   - Supervisor writes to PROJECT_MATRIX.md (requestId dedup)
   - Grafana picks up the new row

3. **Via OpenCode subagent**: When you use `@coder` or other subagents, they can call Craft Anything MCP tools, and the parent session logs the results.

chunks.heading: To ensure Craft Anything data reaches the database:
chunks.text:
### To ensure Craft Anything data reaches the database:
- **Always route through Hermes supervisor** for tracked investigations
- **Use `@researcher` or `@reviewer`** to wrap Craft Anything commands
- **The supervisor writes one row per turn** to Obsidian + Grafana
- **requestId dedup** prevents duplicate entries

chunks.text:
### Example: Tracked Craft Anything investigation
```
@researcher Use Craft Anything to triage suspicious.exe and write a report
# → Hermes routes to @researcher
# → @researcher calls craft-anything-cli triage suspicious.exe
# → @researcher calls craft-anything-cli report --html
# → @researcher writes results to Obsidian Daily (frontmatter + notes)
# → Hermes writes to PROJECT_MATRIX.md (requestId dedup)
# → Grafana dashboard updates with new row
```

chunks.heading: 2nd Brain Summary
chunks.text:
## 2nd Brain Summary

**You already have a second brain.** Your Obsidian vault at `C:\Users\jpowe\Documents\ObsidianVault\` is a fully functional second brain following Tiago Forte's BASB methodology:

1. **Capture**: Daily notes, agent vocabulary, project rows, tool manifests
2. **Organize**: Daily/, Work/, Projects/, Dashboards/, Templates/, mcp/, docker/, docs/, tools/, repos/
3. **Distill**: Agent_Vocabulary.md, Agent_Vocabulary_GrokBot.md, INTEGRATIONS.md
4. **Express**: Grafana dashboards, PROJECT_MATRIX.md, Daily logs, git commits

**Is it useful?** Yes — it's the backbone of your entire system. Every agent reads/writes to it. Grafana scrapes it for live metrics. The REA loop depends on it for tracking progress. Without it, you'd lose context between sessions.

**What makes yours special:** It's not just notes — it's a living database that your AI team reads and writes to automatically. Every turn adds a row. requestId dedup prevents duplicates. The Grafana dashboard turns it into a live monitoring system.

chunks.heading: Template database vs project database
chunks.text:
# Template database vs project database

There are **two separate SQLite files** with the same core schema:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `data/knowledge.db` | The **template** — generic, publishable knowledge about the stack, machine, agents and docs. Safe to pull on any workstation. |
| `projects/polsia-free-v1/knowledge.db` | This project's **own copy**, with the same tables plus project-only evidence, source ledger, build log and approvals. |

The project file is a copy of the template design, not a second copy of the
template's content. It contains only `polsia free v1` data.

A working copy is also written into the project workspace at
`C:\Users\jpowe\Desktop\projects\polsia free v1\.hive\knowledge.db` so the agent
can read it locally without touching the repo.

chunks.heading: Rebuild the project database
chunks.text:
## Rebuild the project database

```powershell
cd C:\Users\jpowe\hive-mind-rea-template
python scripts\build_index.py `
  --root "C:\Users\jpowe\Desktop\projects\polsia free v1" `
  --project `
  --out "C:\Users\jpowe\hive-mind-rea-template\projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db"

Copy-Item projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db `
  "C:\Users\jpowe\Desktop\projects\polsia free v1\.hive\knowledge.db" -Force
```

Run this after a build finishes so screenshots, `capture.json`, `docs-data.js`
and the build log are current.

chunks.heading: Same core schema
chunks.text:
## Same core schema

`documents`, `headings`, `chunks`, `links`, `facts`, `chunks_fts` exist in both.
The project file adds:

| Table | What it guarantees |
|---|---|
| `sources` | One row per file with `sha256`, bytes and modified time — nothing is silently missed or duplicated. `path` is unique. |
| `assets` | Screenshots, fonts and binaries with hash, size and image dimensions. Duplicate files are detectable by identical `sha256`. |
| `runs` | Every `build-activity.log` event (time, kind, text) — the full build history. |
| `approvals` | Every inbox question/approval with answered/waiting status. |

Very large evidence JSON files (14–16 MB in this project) are recorded in
`sources` as `evidence` by hash and size, **not** chunked into FTS. This keeps
the project DB small (~5.6 MB) while still proving the file was seen.

chunks.heading: Query either database
chunks.text:
## Query either database

```powershell
python scripts\query.py --stats
python scripts\query.py --db projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db --stats
python scripts\query.py --db projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db --search "cookie banner"
python scripts\query.py --db projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db --runs 10
python scripts\query.py --db projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db --assets
python scripts\query.py --db projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db --sources

# sqlite-utils is installed for ad-hoc SQL
python -m sqlite_utils projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db tables
python -m sqlite_utils projects\polsia-free-v1\knowledge.db query \
  "select kind, count(*), sum(bytes) from assets group by kind"
```

Useful dedup check:

```sql
SELECT sha256, count(*) copies, group_concat(path)
FROM sources GROUP BY sha256 HAVING copies > 1;
```

chunks.heading: Current limitation — authenticated pages
chunks.text:
## Current limitation — authenticated pages

Craft Anything's `web_site_open` uses a **fresh browser profile with no logins**.
The original target `https://polsia.com/dashboard/untitled-l1v2k8` redirected to
`/login`, so the capture contains only public pages. Any part of the logged-in
dashboard cannot be reproduced from this evidence. Provide screenshots or saved
HTML from a logged-in session, place them under `capture/dashboard/`, rebuild
the project database, and run another refinement round.

A second known gap is functional, not visual: `app/src/studio.js` currently has
a **list of selectable agents**. The requested design is a **single team** whose
members work concurrently, share messages and hand off work like a real
company. That requirement is recorded in `data/build-facts.json` under
`requirements` and must be the subject of the next refinement round.

chunks.heading: Team workflow brief — polsia free v1
chunks.text: # Team workflow brief — polsia free v1

chunks.heading: The correction
chunks.text:
## The correction

The current studio is a **picker**: a list of agents you select one at a time.
That is not what was asked for. The requested system is **one team** that works
together, like a real company or organisation: members have roles, work at the
same time on the same task, and pass information between themselves.

chunks.heading: What to build in `app/`
chunks.text: ## What to build in `app/`

chunks.heading: 1. No picker — the task selects the members
chunks.text:
### 1. No picker — the task selects the members

- **Remove member selection from the UI entirely.** The person types a task and
  presses Go. They never choose who works on it.
- The system automatically selects the right member(s) for that task by role,
  and shows **why** each was chosen ("Matched: research, data analysis, QA").
- Members are visible as a live team roster with status, but clicking one only
  opens their detail — it does not make the system work on only that member.
- Default state after a task is submitted: the selected members work together.

chunks.heading: 2. More than one member is active by default
chunks.text:
### 2. More than one member is active by default

- A task is created once. The orchestrator decomposes it and delegates to
  several members **at the same time**, based on the task's needs.
- **More than one member is always active** unless the task genuinely requires
  only one role. When a single member is selected, the UI explains why
  ("Single-role task: documentation only"). This decision is automatic.
- Members have distinct roles (orchestrator, planner, researcher, engineer,
  reviewer, tester, operations, integration, documentation, support, finance,
  QA, etc.), each with goals, permissions and a live status:
  `idle → working → blocked → handoff → done`.
- Several members must be able to show `working` simultaneously.

chunks.heading: 3. Shared communication (the important part)
chunks.text:
### 3. Shared communication (the important part)

- Implement a **shared message bus** in the browser (event bus + `localStorage`
  persistence, no backend):
  - members post messages to the team channel with `{from, to, taskId, type, body, time}`
  - `to` may be a member id, a role, or `all`
  - a member's output can become another member's input (artefact handoff)
- The UI shows a **team channel** (chronological messages), a **task board**
  (to-do / in progress / review / done with owner and role), and a **handoff
  trail** showing what each member passed to whom.
- Members react to messages addressed to them and to new tasks in their role;
  this is what makes it feel like a team rather than a list.

chunks.heading: 3b. Agents have several languages — support them all
chunks.text:
### 3b. Agents have several languages — support them all

Agents do not all speak the same way, and the team must be efficient. The shared
bus must support **more than five** distinct communication types, label each
message with its type, choose the right one automatically, and let the person
filter the channel by type. Implement at least these:

| # | Language / type | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Natural-language prose | human-readable team channel and summaries |
| 2 | Canonical JSON envelope | `{from,to,taskId,type,body,time,priority}` — the internal wire format |
| 3 | Compact task/intent DSL | short verbs: `TASK`, `ASSIGN`, `ASK`, `ANSWER`, `HANDOFF`, `BLOCKED`, `DONE` |
| 4 | Markdown artefacts | plans, specs and reports passed between roles |
| 5 | Tool/function-call format | `{tool, arguments, result}` for work done by a member |
| 6 | Topic-based events (pub/sub) | `task.created`, `build.failed`, `review.ready` with subscribers |
| 7 | Shared blackboard state | small key/value facts any member can read/write, with versions |
| 8 | Semantic tags / embedding-style summary | compact meaning tags plus a short vector-like digest for fast matching |
| 9 | A2A/MCP-style envelopes | agent-to-agent and tool-result messages compatible with external agents |
| 10 | Human report digest | plain-language round summary for the person (email/chat) |

Rules:
- A message carries a `langua

chunks.heading: 3b. Agents have several languages — support them all
chunks.text:
tool-result messages compatible with external agents |
| 10 | Human report digest | plain-language round summary for the person (email/chat) |

Rules:
- A message carries a `language` field; the UI shows which language was used.
- The router picks the most efficient type for the situation (DSL for control
  messages, JSON for machine handoffs, Markdown for documents, prose for the
  person).
- New languages must be pluggable: a `LANGUAGES` registry, not hard-coded
  `if/else` chains.
- All languages persist to the same local message log and participate in the
  handoff trail.

chunks.heading: 4. Automation and human oversight
chunks.text:
### 4. Automation and human oversight

- Auto mode runs in rounds with intervals: hours, days, weeks, months, years,
  or non-stop. A visible countdown shows the next round.
- The person authorises once. That authorisation is remembered in local state;
  ordinary actions do not ask again. Sensitive actions can still be gated.
- Reports (round summary, messages, decisions, files changed) can be sent to a
  configured email address or chat webhook. No API keys are hard-coded.

chunks.heading: 5. Autonomy — the continuous REA loop
chunks.text:
### 5. Autonomy — the continuous REA loop

Given a task, the team runs this loop **without hand-holding**, and keeps
cycling until the task's acceptance criteria pass or a human-only item blocks it:

| # | Phase | Key | What must happen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Intake + gap analysis | `intake` | Restate the task, write acceptance criteria, list what is known/unknown, identify exactly what is missing and what the user must supply. Produce a gap list with severity. |
| 2 | Plan | `plan` | Decompose the gaps into role-sized jobs, assign owners, set order and dependencies. |
| 3 | Internet + open resources | `discover` | Search the internet for similar builds, prior art, docs and data. Check open-source repos, public datasets and free services. Record each source with a URL and a one-line finding. |
| 4 | Reverse-engineer closed sources | `reverse` | **Byte-by-byte, bit-by-bit sweep** of every available artifact: file ranges, headers, strings, offsets, bundles, network requests, formats and behaviour. Account for **100% of bytes**; anything not understood goes into the unknown ledger with its offset range. Record evidence; never copy proprietary code into `app/`. |
| 5 | Automatic setup | `setup` | Install/configure whatever the build needs: tools, free-tier accounts/endpoints, model providers, storage and integrations. Use free substitutes for paid services (see registry). |
| 6

chunks.heading: 5. Autonomy — the continuous REA loop
chunks.text:
ll/configure whatever the build needs: tools, free-tier accounts/endpoints, model providers, storage and integrations. Use free substitutes for paid services (see registry). |
| 6 | Build | `build` | Produce the first working version from the gathered evidence. |
| 7 | Test | `test` | Run automated checks: build, links, console errors, unit tests, visual comparison. |
| 8 | Check / verify | `check` | Independent review against the acceptance criteria by roles that did not build it. |
| 9 | Fix errors | `fix` | Correct every failure; re-run the failing check. |
| 10 | Amend | `amend` | Improve the result using new evidence: wording, layout, logic, data and missing content. |
| 11 | Implement | `implement` | Integrate the amended work, rebuild and freeze a version. |
| 12 | Report + retrospective | `report` | Write the round report, what changed, what is still blocked, and the next improvement. |
| 13 | Loop | `loop` | If any acceptance criterion fails, return to phase 3 (new evidence) or 6 (rebuild) with a new attempt. Continue until achieved or blocked only on the human gate. |

Rules:

- A task is `done` only when every acceptance criterion passes and the gap
  list is closed. "Good enough" is not a stopping condition.
- Failures never end the loop: retry with a different approach, then hand the
  job to another role if it stays blocked.
- `PHASES` in code must be data-driven

chunks.heading: 5. Autonomy — the continuous REA loop
chunks.text:
stopping condition.
- Failures never end the loop: retry with a different approach, then hand the
  job to another role if it stays blocked.
- `PHASES` in code must be data-driven so new phases can be added without
  rewriting the runner.
- The activity log must show phase, attempt number, evidence used and owner.

chunks.heading: Byte-by-byte reverse-engineering rule (mandatory)
chunks.text:
#### Byte-by-byte reverse-engineering rule (mandatory)

When the `reverse` phase runs, the team must not skim or sample an artifact:

1. Record the artifact's total byte length and sha256 before analysis.
2. Walk it in explicit ranges (headers, tables, strings, code, data, padding),
   keeping an `analysed_bytes` total. `coverage = analysed_bytes / total_bytes`.
3. Every range gets a finding (what it is) or an unknown entry with its offset
   range and why it could not be understood. No silent skipping.
4. A reverse-engineering gap closes only at **100% accounted coverage**, even
   if some ranges are recorded as unknown. Unknowns are carried into the next
   round and re-probed with a different tool or model.
5. Findings must be evidence-backed (offset + hash + observed bytes/output).
   Behavioural claims get a differential replay, not an assumption.
6. Binary/compressed/encrypted regions are still accounted for by range and
   hash; do not attempt DRM circumvention — record them as unknown and stop.

chunks.heading: 5b. Free services instead of paid ones
chunks.text:
### 5b. Free services instead of paid ones

Keep a `FREE_SERVICES` registry that maps a paid capability to a free/open
substitute and uses it automatically unless the user supplies their own:

| Paid capability | Free substitute |
|---|---|
| Search / web data | Marginalia, Hacker News, Wikipedia, direct site fetch, Bing/DDG HTML, user's browser via `browse` MCP |
| LLM inference | Nous free tier models, OpenCode free models, local Ollama fallback |
| Repo / hosting | GitHub free, GitHub Pages, local git |
| Storage / DB | IndexedDB + local SQLite knowledge databases in this repo |
| Diagrams / docs | Mermaid, Markdown, Open XML (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx), CSV, SVG, HTML |
| Email reports | `mailto:` draft plus a user-configured free webhook |
| Payments | Stripe/PayPal **test mode** with the user's own key; no gating of features |
| OCR / PDF / media | Local Python libs already installed (pypdf, Pillow, pandas) |

Every substitute records `substitutesFor`, cost `0`, and a source URL. If a
free option cannot do the job, the team produces a user handoff card instead
of silently failing or buying anything.

chunks.heading: 5c. Human gate — only what the person must do
chunks.text:
### 5c. Human gate — only what the person must do

When a step needs a login, API key, payment credential, irreversible action or
authorisation, the team must not stop the whole loop. It creates a **handoff
card** containing:

- exactly what is needed and why (one short paragraph),
- a numbered click-by-click walkthrough to get it,
- the precise field/link/permission required,
- which task and phase is waiting,
- a "continue without it" fallback if one exists.

All other members keep working on independent gaps. Once the user supplies the
item, the waiting phase resumes automatically. Authorisation given once is
remembered; only sensitive or irreversible actions ask again.

chunks.heading: 5e. Social connections
chunks.text:
### 5e. Social connections

The studio must connect to social platforms, not only display a link to X.
Add a `SOCIAL_CONNECTIONS` registry with at least:

- X/Twitter (already linked in the original), LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram,
  YouTube, TikTok, Reddit, Bluesky, Threads, Pinterest,
- Discord, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp (chat/community),
- GitHub (already an integration) and email.

Each entry has `id`, `name`, `category`, `scopes`, `connectSteps`, `status`
(disconnected / connected / expired), `readOnly` default, and a test-mode
preview. No secret is stored in local state; the person supplies credentials
through their own OAuth flow or a webhook. Reports can be posted to any
connected channel, with human approval remembered once.

chunks.heading: 5f. Dashboard surfaces to reproduce
chunks.text:
### 5f. Dashboard surfaces to reproduce

The studio must expose the same account surfaces seen in the original dashboard:
**Settings, Teams, Refer and earn, Help, Give feedback, Personal account,
Billing, Upgrade, Usage details, Top up credits, Credits, New company, My
portfolio**, plus any other menu items discovered. Each surface needs a real
route, a working state model, and links back to the team workflow. `Credits` and
`Top up credits` must remain informational/test-mode only — no feature may be
locked behind them.

chunks.heading: 5g. Every dashboard button becomes a real, improved action
chunks.text:
### 5g. Every dashboard button becomes a real, improved action

Captured from the authenticated dashboard (`samples/dashboard-evidence/`): 58
clickable controls including `Auto Mode`, `Night task`, `Subscribe`, `Setup
payments`, `Connect Brex`, `Connect Mercury`, `Connect X account`, `Tweet`,
`Delete tweet`, `Cold outreach`, `Support`, `Meta Ads - Not running yet`,
`Image`, `Video`, `New capability`, `New tasks`, `See all tasks`, `Run task: …`,
`Open inbox`, `Refresh`, `View all`, `Edit`, `Pause`, `Review change`,
`Save address`, `Try again`, `Close`, `Logout`, `+ Add credits`, `Credits 0`,
`Top up credits`, `Usage details`, `Upgrade`, `Billing`, `Teams`, `Settings`,
`Personal accounts`, `Help & More`, `Give Feedback`, `Refer & Earn`,
`My Portfolio`, `New Company`, `Notifications` and the menu groups.

Rules for the rebuild:

- No decorative buttons. Every control dispatches a typed action through the
  team message bus and appears in the activity/audit log.
- Each action has `id`, `owner`, `status`, `started`, `finished`, `result`,
  `retryCount` and, where possible, `undo`.
- Destructive or irreversible actions (`Delete tweet`, `Logout`, payments,
  publishing) require remembered human authorisation via the human gate.
- Long actions (`Run task`, `Tweet`, `Setup payments`) show progress and can be
  paused/retried; failures produce `Try again` with the reason.
- Integration b

via the human gate.
- Long actions (`Run task`, `Tweet`, `Setup payments`) show progress and can be
  paused/retried; failures produce `Try again` with the reason.
- Integration buttons (`Connect X`, `Connect Brex`, `Connect Mercury`, Meta Ads,

chunks.heading: 5h. Floating chat with the agents (bottom-right)
chunks.text:
### 5h. Floating chat with the agents (bottom-right)

The original has a chat bubble in the bottom-right corner where the user talks
to the AI agents. The rebuild must include it on every page:

- Fixed bottom-right launch button with an unread badge; opens a chat panel.
- Panel shows a message list with speaker, timestamp, language tag and status,
  plus a composer with Send, attachments placeholder, quick-action chips and a
  typing indicator.
- The person never picks a member: messages are routed through the team message
  bus and the auto-selection logic chooses the responsible members.
- All ten communication languages are supported; the panel can filter them.
- History persists in local state and appears in reports; sensitive requests
  go through the human gate.
- Accessible: labelled button, Escape to close, focus management, keyboard
  send, responsive on mobile with no sideways scroll.

chunks.heading: 5i. Navigation and UI/UX polish
chunks.text:
### 5i. Navigation and UI/UX polish

The rebuild currently looks messy compared with the original. Required:

- A **burger menu** (☰) in the top navigation for narrow screens and as the
  primary collapsed navigation control on every page.
- **Cascading menus** for grouped items (Business capabilities, Media
  capabilities, Billing, Help & More, Notifications). Each group expands on
  click/hover, shows its children indented, and **collapses** when another
  group opens, when the user clicks outside, or on Escape.
- Only one menu group open at a time; expanded state is visible, keyboard
  accessible (Enter/Space/arrow keys), and announced to screen readers.
- Match the original's visual language exactly: monochrome palette, Suisse
  Mono / Editorial fonts, 480px content column, 24/20/12/8px spacing, 2px
  radii, 1440/768/390 breakpoints, no sideways scroll.
- Reduce visual noise: consistent alignment, clear heading hierarchy,
  restrained borders/shadows, deliberate whitespace, and a visible active
  state. Re-run the visual check after navigation changes.

chunks.heading: 5j. Teammates are roles, not AI model names
chunks.text:
### 5j. Teammates are roles, not AI model names

Never name a teammate after an AI model or product (no `hermes`, `claude`,
`codex`, `grok` as identities). Every teammate is a **role**:

`lead`, `research`, `developer`, `coder`, `planner`, `designer`, `tester`,
`reviewer`, `ops`, `security`, `integration`, `docs`, `support`, `finance`,
`legal`, `growth`, `people`, `data`, `qa`, `deploy`, `monitor`.

Each role has `id`, `name`, `description`, `goals`, `permissions`, `status` and
`subRoles`. A separate `ENGINES` registry maps backend agents/models to roles
(Hermes, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, local Ollama, etc.). The person never
sees a model as a teammate; the system assigns the best available engine to a
role at runtime and can swap it without changing the team. This makes the build
model-independent and able to cover any task by adding roles/engines.

chunks.heading: 5k. Near-total autonomy — no "Load & Run" for the user
chunks.text:
### 5k. Near-total autonomy — no "Load & Run" for the user

The user must never have to choose a model, pick a skill, press "Load", or run
a build manually. Add an `AUTONOMOUS_BOOTSTRAP` flow:

1. On open, auto-detect the workspace, existing files, available engines and
   free services; show a short plain-language status, not a technical menu.
2. Auto-select roles and engines, auto-load the right skills, and start the
   13-phase loop from the user's single prompt.
3. Auto-install/configure what is missing through `FREE_SERVICES`, using
   test-mode defaults; no API keys or credits required.
4. Auto-verify after every phase (build, links, behaviour, visual check) and
   auto-fix failures; only surface an item when it truly needs a human.
5. The only user inputs are: the task, optional credentials/authorisation via
   the human gate, and feedback. Everything technical is handled internally.
6. Show a simple progress view ("Planning → Researching → Building →
   Checking → Done") with plain words, and a chat box for follow-ups.

chunks.heading: 5l. All capabilities and protocols, free by default
chunks.text:
### 5l. All capabilities and protocols, free by default

Add a `CAPABILITIES` registry where every capability has a free/open default
and an optional paid tier using the person's own key. No feature is locked.

| Capability | Free default | Optional paid |
|---|---|---|
| Text / chat / reasoning | Nous free, OpenCode free, local Ollama | user's API key |
| Embeddings / search | local SQLite FTS5, BM25 | hosted vector DB |
| Speech-to-text / voice recognition | local faster-whisper, Web Speech | hosted STT |
| Text-to-speech | Edge TTS, browser SpeechSynthesis | hosted TTS |
| Image generation | local SVG/Canvas, bundled icons | image API |
| Audio / music generation | local synthesis, Web Audio | music API |
| Video generation | local render via ffmpeg/Canvas | video API |
| OCR / document reading | pypdf, Pillow, local OCR | hosted OCR |
| Email | local `mailto:` drafts + IMAP/SMTP via user config | hosted mail |
| Phone assistant | WebRTC/SIP test mode with local STT/TTS | telephony provider |
| Diagrams / charts | Mermaid, `scripts/viz.py` | hosted diagramming |
| MCP tools | any stdio/HTTP MCP server, allowlisted | hosted MCP |
| Protocols | MCP, A2A, Agent Skills, webhooks, IMAP/SMTP, HTTP | enterprise connectors |

Rules:

- `CAPABILITIES` entries carry `id`, `name`, `freeProvider`, `paidProvider`,
  `status`, `cost`, `consent`, `testMode`.
- `MCP_SERVERS` registry suppor

chunks.text:
rprise connectors |

Rules:

- `CAPABILITIES` entries carry `id`, `name`, `freeProvider`, `paidProvider`,
  `status`, `cost`, `consent`, `testMode`.
- `MCP_SERVERS` registry supports add/remove/enable, tool discovery and a

- `ENGINES` supports free and paid models; switching never changes the team's

chunks.heading: 6. Payments (commerce, not feature gates)
chunks.text:
### 6. Payments (commerce, not feature gates)

- The app must be able to **take payments** for real transactions through a
  payment provider the person configures (e.g. Stripe or PayPal, test mode by
  default): create an invoice/checkout, record the transaction, issue a receipt.
- This is **not** a subscription, credit system or paywall. No feature, core,
  module or function may require payment to activate. The earlier requirement
  "no paid feature gates" still wins.
- Never hard-code keys or treat a payment as permission to use a feature.

chunks.heading: 7. Self-improvement of delivery
chunks.text:
### 7. Self-improvement of delivery

- At the end of each round the team writes a short **retrospective** into local
  state: what failed, what was retried, what worked, what to change next time.
- Track a simple completion metric (tasks done / attempted, retries, blocked
  items) and show it in the UI.
- Failed tasks go back on the board with a different owner or approach instead
  of disappearing.

chunks.heading: 8. Constraints
chunks.text:
### 8. Constraints

- Keep the captured visual design: same fonts, 480 px column, breakpoints,
  monochrome palette and no sideways scroll on phone.
- No subscription, credits, tokens-to-buy or paid feature gates anywhere.
- Everything runs locally in the browser unless the person configures their own
  endpoint. Do not paste the original site's code into `app/`.
- Only edit files inside `app/`. Build with `npm run build` until `dist/` is
  produced, then run the Craft Anything visual check and fix what it reports.

chunks.heading: Acceptance criteria
chunks.text:
## Acceptance criteria

1. There is **no control to pick a member**. The person only enters a task and
   presses Go.
2. Submitting a normal task automatically activates **more than one** member;
   each shows `working` at the same time, with a visible reason for selection.
3. A single member is active only for genuinely single-role tasks, and the UI
   says why. This is automatic, not chosen by the person.
4. A message from one member appears in the shared channel and can be addressed
   to another member, who responds or produces a handoff artefact.
5. The task board updates automatically as work moves between members.
6. Authorisation is requested once, then remembered.
7. Auto-mode interval selector includes hours/days/weeks/months/years/non-stop.
8. A task runs the full 13-phase REA loop (intake/gap analysis → plan →
   discover internet+open resources → reverse-engineer closed sources →
   automatic setup → build → test → check → fix → amend → implement → report →
   loop) without manual steps. It keeps cycling until every acceptance
   criterion passes or a human-only item is handed off.
9. A payment integration can create a test-mode checkout and record it, while
   no feature is locked behind payment.
10. Each round produces a retrospective and a visible completion metric.
11. At least ten communication languages/types are supported, each message is
   labelled with it
