chunks.heading: Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
# Troubleshooting

Symptom first. Every entry here was hit on a real machine and fixed.

---

chunks.heading: The agent stops mid-prompt and never finishes
chunks.text:
## The agent stops mid-prompt and never finishes

**Not an MCP problem.** The local stack is almost always healthy; the failure is upstream.

Check, in order:

1. `python scripts/doctor.py` — if no `[fail]` lines, the local side is fine.
2. Provider balance. The reference failure was:
   ```
   AI.Error: Insufficient balance. Top up at https://opencode.ai/console/...
   ```
   Topping up, or switching to a local model, resolves it.
3. Test with a local model to prove the rest of the chain:
   ```bash
   opencode --model ollama/lfm3:1.7b
   ```

---

chunks.heading: An MCP server closes immediately
chunks.text: ## An MCP server closes immediately

chunks.heading: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from `npx`
chunks.text:
### `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from `npx`

A corrupted npx cache. The package graph is incomplete, so the child process exits
before the MCP session proves healthy.

```bash
rm -rf ~/AppData/Local/npm-cache/_npx/*   # Windows
rm -rf ~/.npm/_npx/*                      # macOS / Linux
npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 --version         # must print a version
```

Then restart the host (Hermes / OpenCode).

chunks.heading: `${SOME_VAR}` in a config is never substituted
chunks.text:
### `${SOME_VAR}` in a config is never substituted

MCP configs pass `${VAR}` through to the child process environment. If the variable is
unset the child may fail silently. Set it at user scope:

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON", (Get-Command python).Source, "User")
```

```bash
export REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON="$(which python3)"
```

---

chunks.heading: `pip` is broken
chunks.text:
## `pip` is broken

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pip._vendor.rich._emoji_codes'
```

Repair in place — no need to reinstall Python:

```bash
python -m ensurepip --upgrade
python -m pip install --user pwntools
```

---

chunks.heading: A tool says "not installed" but it clearly is
chunks.text:
## A tool says "not installed" but it clearly is

GUI installers routinely do not add themselves to `PATH`. Both `doctor.py` and
`bootstrap.py` probe conventional install roots before reporting a miss:

- Windows: `C:\Program Files\Craft Anything`, `C:\Program Files\Ollama`
- macOS: `/Applications/Craft Anything.app/Contents/MacOS`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`
- Linux: `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin`

If a tool lives somewhere else, put it on `PATH` or symlink it into one of those roots.

---

chunks.heading: Hermes: `No __init__.py` when loading a plugin
chunks.text:
## Hermes: `No __init__.py` when loading a plugin

Some v3 plugins are dashboard-only and ship no Python package. Either add a minimal
`__init__.py`:

```python
__version__ = "3.0.0"
```

…or disable the plugin. The dashboard mounts from `dashboard/api.py` either way.

---

chunks.heading: Stale locks after moving a checkout
chunks.text:
## Stale locks after moving a checkout

This is why runtime state is git-ignored. If you see `*.lock`, `state.db`,
`gateway.lock` or `ticker_heartbeat` inside a commit, the repo is broken for every
machine that clones it. Remove them from the index, keep them on disk:

```bash
git rm --cached -r $(git ls-files | grep -E '\.lock$|state\.db|/logs/|/cache/')
```

Never delete the working copy — only the index entry.

---

chunks.heading: Two Obsidian vaults, notes going missing
chunks.text:
## Two Obsidian vaults, notes going missing

A split second brain. Obsidian cannot merge them for you.

1. Pick the canonical vault (`obsidian-vault/` in the repo by convention).
2. Copy only `*.md` across. Do **not** copy `.obsidian/` — workspace state is per machine.
3. Archive the old vault; do not keep it open in Obsidian.

---

chunks.heading: Out of disk space
chunks.text:
## Out of disk space

Order of operations, largest win first:

1. Docker images — `docker system prune -a` (often 10 GB+). Stop the daemon if unused.
2. WinSxS + Windows Update cache — `tools/repair-windows-admin.ps1`, elevated.
3. Model weights you do not use — `ollama rm <model>`.
4. Temp directories.
5. `hiberfil.sys` — `powercfg /h off` frees roughly your RAM in size, but you lose hibernate.

---

chunks.heading: The laptop is slow with an agent running
chunks.text:
## The laptop is slow with an agent running

On 8 GB of RAM this is expected, and no driver update changes it. In order:

1. Run **one** model at a time.
2. Close browsers before a session (Chrome alone can hold 1.5 GB).
3. Stop Docker unless you need the containers.
4. Check `Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select -First 10`.
5. If `Memory Compression` is above ~500 MB, you are thrashing — nothing else will help
   except adding RAM.

Minimum useful upgrade on this class of laptop: 8 GB SODIMM to reach 12–16 GB.

---

chunks.heading: Commit charge is higher than physical RAM before you open anything
chunks.text:
## Commit charge is higher than physical RAM before you open anything

Symptom: right after a reboot, `(Get-Counter '\Memory\Committed Bytes')` reports more
than installed RAM, and every `Get-CimInstance` / `DISM` / `SFC` call fails with
`0x8007000e` (not enough memory resources).

The cause is services that start automatically, not the applications you launch.
Measure before changing anything:

```powershell
Get-Process | Group-Object ProcessName |
  ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{
      Name = $_.Name; N = $_.Count
      MB   = [math]::Round((($_.Group | Measure-Object PrivateMemorySize64 -Sum).Sum)/1MB, 0)
  } } | Sort-Object MB -Descending | Select-Object -First 15
```

Then `tools/trim-services.ps1` — report only, then `-Apply -StopNow`. Tier 1 has no
functional tradeoff; Tier 2 (PostgreSQL stack, Codex sandbox) means starting those
yourself. Real result on an 8 GB laptop: 15 services moved to Manual, 14.9 GB → 9.9 GB.

chunks.heading: Three things that look like startup entries but are not
chunks.text:
### Three things that look like startup entries but are not

**Packaged services refuse `Set-Service` even when elevated.** `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex`
answers `Access is denied`. Its security descriptor grants only Authenticated Users and the
package SID — Administrators are not in it. The registry holds the same value and *is*
writable when elevated:

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<ServiceName>' -Name Start -Value 3
```

`2` = Automatic, `3` = Manual, `4` = Disabled. `trim-services.ps1` falls back to this
automatically. Restart is not required; `sc.exe stop <name>` applies it now.

**Windows reopens your apps at sign-in.** If processes come back with `sihost.exe` as parent
and there is no `Run` entry, it is app restore, not autostart:

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon' -Name RestartApps -Value 0
```

**`vmmemWSL` is a virtual machine, not a program.** WSL2 defaults to half of physical RAM and
does not return it at idle. Cap it in `%USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig`, then `wsl --shutdown`:

```ini
[wsl2]
memory=2GB
processors=2
swap=1GB
```

On the reference machine that alone released 2.9 GB.

chunks.heading: Claude Vocabulary — How It Maps To Our Hive Mind
chunks.text:
# Claude Vocabulary — How It Maps To Our Hive Mind

*Every term is a Hermes Bot + OpenCode subagent skill, not just a label. Supervisor routes, workers do.*

| Term you named | What Claude means it is | What it is in our stack |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **loop engineering** | Dynamic Workflow JS: `agent()` spawns one subagent; `parallel()` fans out; `pipeline()` streams each item. Failure modes combated: agentic laziness, self-preferential bias, goal drift | Hermes `message_agent(target="coder")` + OpenCode `subagent` tool + Grafana `requestId` dedupe |
| **claude-red** | Red-team harness — untrusted input (Slack tickets) goes to reader agents with read-only tools, never writes/commits | @researcher = read-only, @windows = high-privilege actor only sees summaries |
| **replay theater** | Replaying sessions / trajectories to debug — `state.db` + logs | Hermes `replay` verb regenerates TUI history from state.db |
| **terminal browser** | In-editor terminal pane + browser control | Hermes `browser_exec` (local Chromium) + `terminal local` |
| **reflect** | Post-turn `/reflect` summarises what went wrong | `PROJECT_MATRIX.md` gaps → `SOUL.md` update `/skill` |
| **blast radius** | Scope of a change — file, module, service, fleet | Coders get `worktree` isolation, reviewers get `read` only |
| **cache tax** | Prompt caching cost when you rewrite past context mid-conversation (Hermes in

chunks.heading: Claude Vocabulary — How It Maps To Our Hive Mind
chunks.text:
odule, service, fleet | Coders get `worktree` isolation, reviewers get `read` only |
| **cache tax** | Prompt caching cost when you rewrite past context mid-conversation (Hermes invariant: mutating past context swaps toolsets and multiplies cost, only compression is exception) | Supervisor delegates, never rewrites. Use `/compress` only. |
| **filetree** | File map, filetree `/tree` understanding | `filetread` + `glob` + `grep` tools via OpenClaw Node |
| **you should know** | Claude’s 4 knowledges: subagents vs workflows, skills vs MCP, hooks vs CLI, cost vs quality | Hermes Bot Mode roster covers all 4: `@coder` (subagent), `@beam/@longcat-2-5` (workflow), `@researcher` (skills), `cost_guard` |
| **claude skins** | Pure data `SkinConfig` — colors, spinner faces, thinking verbs | Hermes `display.skin` in `config.yaml`, key-by-key table |
| **savvy progress** | Headway widget — task sub-progress on redirected prints | Hermes `display` progress HUD, `orchestrated progress footer` |
| **mods** | Claude Code Mods — Data sette, Loom, Obfuscator, Operator Mode, VibeSec | Hermes equivalents: `plugins/model-providers/ollama-cloud`, `plugins/memory/obsidian-memory`, `plugins/delegation/default`, `plugins/post_update/`, Kanban |
| **context 7** | Long-window filetree `/tree`/`context7` reading | `context_length: 1000000` in Hermes config, `optimise` prune |
| **skill ui** | Desktop `Ski

chunks.heading: Claude Vocabulary — How It Maps To Our Hive Mind
chunks.text:
_update/`, Kanban |
| **context 7** | Long-window filetree `/tree`/`context7` reading | `context_length: 1000000` in Hermes config, `optimise` prune |
| **skill ui** | Desktop `Skills` lane in `ui-tui/src/app/` | Local `skills/` folder at HERMES_HOME/skills/ |
| **vibeSec** | Vibecoding security tag — `/security audit`, OSV.dev for venv/plugins/MCP | `hermes security audit` in your setup |
| **supabase** | Common MCP server (`mcp_catalog.py`, `mcp.json`) | Connect Supabase MCP → Hermes can query tables (`supabase/mcp.json` catalog) |
| **playwright** | Browser tool primitive | Hermes `tools/builtin/browser` → read `mcp.json` for Playwright MCP |
| **claude-content-skills** | Declarative skill wrappers — content creation micro-tasks (`/review-pr`, `/deploy-staging`) | Local `skills/` + OpenCode `@writer`/`@marketer` |

chunks.heading: How the hive runs this loop
chunks.text:
## How the hive runs this loop

```
Plan → Design → Build → Check → Research → Recheck → Build → Fix → Amend → Compare
 → Feedback → Fine-tune → Plan → Build → Discovery → Test → Compare
 → Gather data → Weakness/Gaps → Improve → Next version
```

Every step writes one row to `Daily/2026-11-09.md` + `Work/Project.md` + `Work/PROJECT_MATRIX.md` frontmatter (`requestId, tokens_total, cost_usd, risk(laya)`). Grafana scrapes Pros + Daily notes to build live matrix. **No duplicate requestId = no duplicate work.**

*Top pick local:* `bonsai-2:4b` (1.6GB, 256K, vision+tools+thinking) — unlimited tokens, 8-12 tok/s on i3-1005G1. Escalate cloud free models once/day (token heavy) when `is_risky>0.8`.

# Grok Bot Terms & Skills — Added to Hive Mind

*Grok Bot Teams are the xAI equivalent of Hermes Bot Mode. Same pattern, different product words. All map to bots you already have.*

| Grok term | Hermes equivalent (what you have) |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|
| **Bot / Agent** | Hermes profile = `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/` (isolated config/memory/skills/chat) — one process serves many profiles, `HERMES_HOME` scoped |
| **Team / Group Chat** | Hermes Bot Mode — 2-6 Bots, 3 serial rounds, `message_agent(target="@coder")` fire-and-forget |
| **Roster** | Hermes Bots pane — avatar, latest msg, unread, Activity now |
| **Routines** | Hermes cron `[bot:<name>] <routine>` — "summarize inbox 09:00" docked beside Bot Chat |
| **@mention** | `@coder hello` in any chat → composer autocomplete → teammate composes own message (your text never forwarded verbatim) |
| **Poll / Pin / Set Reminder** | Polls, pins, reminders = built-in tools in Hermes Bot Chat composer (`/poll`, `/pin`, `/remind`) |
| **Imagine** | `image.generate` plugin (FAL.ai / Replicate) — Hermes `image_gen_provider.py` |
| **Deep Search / Deeper Search** | `web_search` tool + `hermes research` skill — fan-out + adversarial verify |
| **Character / Personas / Rankings** | `SOUL.md` per Bot, `DEFAULT_SOUL.md` may be auto-written by Hermes |
| **Memory** | Hermes `MemoryProvider` ABC (`agent/memory_prov

verify |

chunks.heading: Per-conversation prompt caching (sacred)
chunks.text:
## Per-conversation prompt caching (sacred)
Mutating past context / swapping toolsets mid-conversation breaks cached prefix (multiplies cost). Slash commands that change system-prompt state defer to next session unless `--now`. Our delegation (message_agent/subagent) avoids this via fresh child sessions. Compression (`/compress`) is the only OK.

chunks.heading: 2026-11-19 - Memory pressure, BIOS, and a portable research toolkit
chunks.text: # 2026-11-19 - Memory pressure, BIOS, and a portable research toolkit

chunks.heading: Problem
chunks.text:
## Problem

The laptop was not slow because of drivers. Right after boot it committed
**14.9 GB on 7.7 GB of physical RAM**, so every `Get-CimInstance`, `DISM` and
`SFC` call failed with `0x8007000e` (not enough memory resources).

chunks.heading: Root causes found
chunks.text:
## Root causes found

| Cause | Size | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `vmmemWSL` holding half of RAM | 2.9 GB | `.wslconfig` capped at 2 GB + `wsl --shutdown` |
| 15 auto-start services | ~2.8 GB | `tools/trim-services.ps1 -Tier 2 -Apply -StopNow` |
| Windows reopening apps at sign-in | 1.1 GB | `RestartApps = 0` |
| Codex sandbox service | 1.2 GB | registry `Start = 3` (Set-Service is denied) |

chunks.heading: Result
chunks.text:
## Result

```
commit   14.9 GB -> 9.5 GB      (-36%)
free RAM  0.66 GB -> 1.44 GB
processes    358 -> 268
```

chunks.heading: Findings worth remembering
chunks.text:
## Findings worth remembering

- **Packaged services refuse `Set-Service` even elevated.** Their security
  descriptor grants only Authenticated Users and the package SID. The registry
  value `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\Start` is writable, and
  `3` means Manual.
- **`sihost.exe` as a parent process means app restore, not autostart.** There
  is no Run key to find. `HKCU\...\WinNT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\RestartApps = 0`.
- **Search engines block scripts but not browsers.** Google needs JavaScript,
  Bing returns unrelated filler, DuckDuckGo serves a bot challenge, and no
  public SearXNG instance answered. A real browser gets through every one.

chunks.heading: Hardware
chunks.text:
## Hardware

- **RAM**: Lenovo PSREF confirms *"Up to 12GB (4GB soldered + 8GB SO-DIMM)
  DDR4-2666"*, one slot. Current: 4GB Samsung soldered + 4GB Crucial
  `CT4G4SFS8266` in the slot. Replace the Crucial with 8GB.
- **BIOS**: running `EMCN42WW` (2020-10-28). Latest is **`EMCN60WW`**
  (2024-05-27): https://download.lenovo.com/consumer/mobiles/emcn60ww.exe
  Changelog: CVE-2023-32282, plus Intel microcode updates and ~20 more CVEs
  across 57-59. Applies to 14IIL05 / 15IIL05 / 17IIL05 / V17-IIL.
- **8GB DDR4-2666 SODIMM, UK, 2026-11-19**: Timetec £51.99, Origin Storage
  (Ebuyer) £58.00, Integral £60.95, Mr Memory £62.40, Crucial CT8G4SFS8266
  £63.00. DDR4 is end-of-life, so prices are roughly 2-3x what they were in 2024.

chunks.heading: Built
chunks.text:
## Built

- `tools/trim-services.ps1` - tiered service trimming with `-StopNow`
- `tools/repair-windows-admin.ps1` - SFC/DISM/WinSxS/driver maintenance
- `scripts/research.py` - key-free search, fetch, Hacker News, Wikipedia
- `scripts/office.py` - JSON/Markdown to xlsx/docx/pptx/csv
- `scripts/viz.py` - SVG bar/line/pie charts, Mermaid flowcharts and mindmaps
- `docs/AGENT-ACTIONS.md` - read/write/buy/sell contract for any agent
- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` - symptom-first fixes, all from real failures

chunks.heading: Tooling installed
chunks.text:
## Tooling installed

- `browse` 0.1.5 - browser control, registered with OpenCode, Claude Code,
  Codex, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, LM Studio and Hermes.
  Relay on port 19988. **Extension still needs pairing in the browser.**
- Python: `openpyxl`, `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `youtube-transcript-api`,
  `pwntools` 4.15.1, `pypdf`.
- Repaired: `pip` (corrupted vendor dir), `typing_extensions`, `idna`.

chunks.heading: Still open
chunks.text:
## Still open

- BIOS flash not performed - needs a human to run the Lenovo EXE and reboot.
- RAM not purchased - recommendation above.
- `graphify` and `demobase` **do not exist on this machine**. They are listed as
  optional, disabled layers in `core/stack.yaml`. Do not pretend otherwise.
- Three Obsidian vaults still exist; this note was written to the repo vault and
  mirrored to `Documents\ObsidianVault`.

chunks.heading: Lesson
chunks.text:
## Lesson

Measure commit charge before blaming drivers. A machine that has already spent
its RAM on services cannot install the driver that would have fixed it.

chunks.heading: 2026-11-23 - Idle commit hogs, GitHub credential audit
chunks.text: # 2026-11-23 - Idle commit hogs, GitHub credential audit

chunks.heading: Problem
chunks.text:
## Problem

Three days after the 2026-11-19 fix, commit charge had climbed back to
**17.9 GB of a 20.2 GB limit** (free physical 1.07 GB). The 2026-11-19
trim was still in place, so something else was holding commit.

chunks.heading: Root causes found
chunks.text:
## Root causes found

| Cause | Commit held | Autostart? | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ollama app` + `ollama serve`, **no model loaded** | 3.6 GB | Startup folder `Ollama.lnk` | Stopped, shortcut moved to backup (Tier 2 = on demand) |
| `ChatGPT.exe` = **OpenAI.Codex package**, 14 processes | 1.17 GB | **None** | Killed; no respawn in 75 s |
| Microsoft Copilot app, 9 processes | ~0.3 GB | None found | Killed; no respawn in 100 s |
| Unresponsive `SystemSettings` window | 0.19 GB | n/a | Killed |

chunks.heading: The "ChatGPT returns after reboot" theory was wrong
chunks.text:
### The "ChatGPT returns after reboot" theory was wrong

The 14 `ChatGPT.exe` processes are the **Codex** MSIX package
(`OpenAI.Codex_26.1111.9664.0`). Evidence against an autostart:

- manifest startup task: `Enabled="false"`
- no `Run` / `RunOnce` value, no Startup folder entry
- no scheduled task, no service dependency
- `RestartApps = 0` present and effective
- start time 19/11 17:26:18 = **5 minutes after boot**, not at sign-in
  (a startup task fires within seconds)

It had simply been left running. Killed, nothing restarted it.

chunks.heading: Result
chunks.text:
## Result

```
commit     17.9 GB -> 12.2 GB
free RAM   1.07 GB -> 1.50 GB
```

Residual 12.2 GB is mostly legitimate: Chrome 2.3 GB + Edge 1.2 GB (open
tabs), OpenCode 1.0 GB (this agent), vmmemWSL 0.48 GB.

chunks.heading: GitHub credential audit
chunks.text:
## GitHub credential audit

`cmdkey /list` had 4 GitHub targets. Reading them via `CredRead` (not
`cmdkey`, which cannot show secrets) showed **two distinct live tokens**:

| Target | Token | Scopes | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git:https://github.com` | `gho_XxIp…` | repo, workflow, gist, org, … | **kept** (git works) |
| `git:https://jayprophit@github.com` | `gho_XxIp…` (same) | same | deleted |
| `GitHub for Visual Studio - …` | `gho_XxIp…` (same) | same | deleted |
| `GitHub - https://api.github.com/jayprophit` | `gho_hV2Y…` (different) | repo, user, workflow | deleted |

- The earlier "no entries left" result was a **false negative**: I used
  `Select-String -Pattern 'Target:.*github' -SimpleMatch`, which searches
  for that literal string. Lesson: never combine a regex with `-SimpleMatch`.
- `gho_hV2Y…` was printed during the audit, so it is treated as exposed:
  entry deleted locally, **revoke the issuing OAuth app on GitHub**.
- The originally leaked `gho_zjsFDSeR…` (2026-11-19) is already revoked.

chunks.heading: Still needs elevation / a human
chunks.text:
## Still needs elevation / a human

- Intel telemetry services `ESRV_SVC_QUEENCREEK` (198 MB) and `UDCService`
  (126 MB): `Set-Service` returned **Access is denied** from this shell.
- `AnyDesk` and `TeamViewer` both run Auto (~67 MB). Left alone - stopping
  remote access without asking could lock the user out.
- BIOS updated to EMCN60WW (was EMCN42WW) - verified done via Win32_BIOS.
- RAM still 8 GB; 8 GB DDR4-2666 SO-DIMM not bought.
- Craft Anything's builder is **stopped**: it was spinning in a retry loop.
  No build progress was lost (it had made none).

chunks.heading: Craft Anything ↔ Hermes - the real cause of "nothing happened"
chunks.text:
## Craft Anything ↔ Hermes - the real cause of "nothing happened"

Earlier in this session we assumed the MCP link was broken. The records say otherwise.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 06:01:43 | Builder run starts |
| 06:12:09 | `custom didn't respond in time on any of 3 attempts` - local provider `127.0.0.1:11434` down (Ollama stopped) |
| 06:12:17 | Hermes exits 2, `0 tokens in / 0 out` |
| 06:12:49 | Craft Anything retries automatically |
| 06:33:24 | `Gateway disconnected` again; retry loop every ~90s |

Causes and fixes:

1. **Provider down.** Ollama had been stopped for RAM. Hermes' `model.provider:
   custom` = `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`, so all calls failed. Fixed: use
   `tools/agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider`.
2. **Wrong model for an agent.** `bonsai-2:4b` has `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}` - no
   chat template. Measured: 57.7 s and ~200 hidden tokens to answer "OK".
   `laya` returns HTTP 400 on chat. Fixed: `hermes config set model.default lfm3:1.7b`
   (verified: "OK" in 20.8 s).
3. **Concurrent Hermes runs collide.** Craft Anything retries; manual `-z` tests
   share one gateway. Rule: one builder at a time (`docs/MCP-WIRING.md`).

MCP itself was never broken: `hermes mcp test craft-anything` - connected in
3.9 s, **38 tools** discovered.

Preflight results (2026-11-23): 7/7 PASS. MCP handshake: 38 tools. OpenCode:
`mcp.craft-anything` enabled. Hermes: `craft-anyth

chunks.heading: Craft Anything ↔ Hermes - the real cause of "nothing happened"
chunks.text:
ing` - connected in
3.9 s, **38 tools** discovered.

Preflight results (2026-11-23): 7/7 PASS. MCP handshake: 38 tools. OpenCode:
`mcp.craft-anything` enabled. Hermes: `craft-anything` enabled. Model:
`lfm3:1.7b`. `data/knowledge.db`: 107 documents, 388 chunks, 173 headings.

chunks.heading: Never do again
chunks.text:
## Never do again

- Do not assume a process name identifies an app: `ChatGPT.exe` was Codex.
- Do not trust an empty `cmdkey` filter; verify with `CredRead` and a real
  auth call.
- `commit`, not working set, is the metric that matters on an 8 GB / 20 GB
  pagefile machine. `ollama app` showed 21 MB WS but 3.6 GB commit.

chunks.heading: Craft Anything ↔ Hermes - 15 minutes of silence
chunks.text:
## Craft Anything ↔ Hermes - 15 minutes of silence

The user's builder ran for ~30 minutes and produced **zero app changes**.
Evidence from `build-activity.log` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\agent.log`:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 06:01:43 | build run starts |
| 06:12:09 | `custom didn't respond in time on any of 3 attempts`; exit 2, 0 tokens |
| 06:12:49 | Craft Anything retries automatically |
| 06:21:33 | `Gateway disconnected`; run killed mid-wait |
| 06:29:19 | retry; a second 9,096-char session competes with the first |
| 06:33:24 | same error; loop keeps restarting every ~90 s |

chunks.heading: Root causes (MCP was NOT one of them)
chunks.text:
### Root causes (MCP was NOT one of them)

- **Provider down.** Ollama had been stopped in the memory cleanup above.
  Hermes points at `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`, so all calls timed out.
- **Model unfit for an agent.** `bonsai-2:4b` has `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}` —
  no chat template. Measured: 57.7 s and ~200 hidden tokens to say "OK";
  empty content below 64 tokens. `laya` returns HTTP 400 on chat completions.
- **Concurrent one-shots.** Two Hermes runs share one gateway; the second
  gets `Gateway disconnected; turn outcome is unknown`.

`hermes mcp test craft-anything` proved MCP fine: connected in 3.9 s,
**38 tools discovered**. `hermes mcp list` shows it enabled.

chunks.heading: Fix applied
chunks.text:
### Fix applied

- `hermes config set model.default lfm3:1.7b` (tool-calling, 15.8–20.8 s per
  short reply; real turn: 2,050 in / 34 out in 46.3 s). Backup of config kept.
- Killed the self-retrying `craft-anything.exe` loop; no progress was lost.
- Added `tools/agent-preflight.ps1` (7/7 PASS here) and
  `tools/wire-craft-anything.ps1`, `docs/MCP-WIRING.md`.
- Added `data/` knowledge base: `build-facts.json`, `index.json`,
  `knowledge.db` (SQLite FTS5, 107 docs / 388 chunks / 123 facts),
  `scripts/build_index.py`, `scripts/query.py`.

chunks.heading: Decision for the desktop
chunks.text:
### Decision for the desktop

On 8 GB CPU-only, use OpenCode (cloud model) for multi-step builds; Hermes with
a local 1.7B cannot prefill a 9k prompt plus 38 tool schemas inside the gateway
window. With 16 GB+ / GPU on the desktop, a 7B–14B local model is viable.
Run `agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider` on any workstation before a build.

chunks.heading: Free cloud models - final decision
chunks.text:
## Free cloud models - final decision

The local setup worked but was too slow, so all three tools now use **free cloud
models**. Probed live from the Nous inference API before choosing:

| Model | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free` | tool call OK; 9k prompt in 2.6 s | Hermes |
| `opencode/hy4-flash-free` | `opencode run` OK in 2.7 s, no credits | OpenCode + Craft Anything builder |
| `tencent/hy4-flash:free`, `upstage/solar-mini4:free`, `meituan/longcat-2.5:free` | no usable tool calls | rejected |
| `qwen/qwen4-max:free` | upstream capacity errors | rejected |
| all paid Nous models | HTTP 404: no credits | unavailable |

Config changes:
- Hermes: `provider: nous`, `base_url: https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1`,
  `model.default` and both auxiliary models = `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free`.
- OpenCode: `"model": "opencode/hy4-flash-free"` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`;
  MCP entries preserved. Backups kept for both config files.
- Craft Anything: `craft.json` `"builder": "OpenCode"`; CLI runs used
  `--backend OpenCode`. `craft-anything-cli doctor` = healthy, MCP self-test 38 tools.
- Ollama is no longer needed for agents and can be stopped for ~3.6 GB commit.
- Never copy a Nous token into the repo or a config file; Hermes refreshes its own.

chunks.heading: Build outcome so far
chunks.text:
### Build outcome so far
- First CLI run built the Vite site (`app/`, `dist/` 9 files) and reached

- That run was killed by a 600 s tool timeout; the user restarted Craft Anything

- One transient tool error (`craft-anything_rebuild_status` missing `project`)

chunks.heading: Project database + the team correction
chunks.text:
## Project database + the team correction

- Generalized `scripts/build_index.py`: `--root`, `--out`, `--project`.
- Template DB: `data/knowledge.db` (109 docs, 420 chunks, 141 facts, 1.1 MB).
- Project DB: `projects/polsia-free-v1/knowledge.db` (same core schema + assets,

- `sources` gives one sha256 per file, so nothing is duplicated or missed.
  Two 14-16 MB evidence JSON files are recorded by hash, not chunked.
- Installed `sqlite-utils` 4.2.1; PIL already present for image dimensions.
- **User correction:** the studio is a picker of individual agents, but the

chunks.heading: Team brief refined (user clarification)
chunks.text:
### Team brief refined (user clarification)
- No picker at all: the task auto-selects the right member(s) with a reason.
- More than one member active by default; single member only when genuinely
  needed, decided automatically.
- Must work autonomously: plan, research, build, test, fix, report; resolve
  blockers and hand off failed steps to another role.
- Must be able to take payments for real transactions (test mode, user's key)
  but with **no** subscription, credits or paid feature gates.
- Each round writes a retrospective and a completion metric.
- `docs/TEAM-BRIEF.md` is the authoritative spec; a controlled follow-up build
  was launched with it after stopping the GUI retry loop.

chunks.heading: Verified final build (09:50)
chunks.text:
### Verified final build (09:50)
- `npm run build` succeeds: 15 dist files, 7 page folders including the new
  `/changelog` and `/acceptable-use`.
- `app/src/studio.js` is 951 lines: no member picker, automatic role selection
  with reasons, multiple members active concurrently, shared message bus,
  task board, handoffs, autonomy loop, payments tab with no paid gates,
  retrospectives, auto-mode intervals and remembered authorisation.
- Ten inter-agent communication languages implemented as a pluggable registry
  (prose, JSON envelope, task DSL, Markdown, tool calls, pub/sub events,
  blackboard, semantic digest, A2A/MCP envelopes, human digest); every message
  is labelled, auto-routed, filterable and persisted.
- Visual check: 78% alike, 30/30 claims hold. Remaining visual gaps are in the
  long legal pages (/privacy 64%, /terms 62%) and a missing form field.
- Authenticated dashboard still cannot be reproduced: Craft Anything's browser
  has no logins and the target redirected to `/login`. Need logged-in evidence.
- Two concurrent builders once overwrote each other; stale trees were killed
  and a final controlled single round produced the state above.

chunks.heading: Gap analysis and REA loop expansion (10:07)
chunks.text:
## Gap analysis and REA loop expansion (10:07)

Gaps found against the requested autonomy loop: the old `PHASES` had only
7 stages (plan, research, build, test, check, fix, report) and no internet/open
resource scan, no closed-source reverse engineering, no setup, no explicit
gap analysis, no amend/implement, no "loop until criteria pass", no free-service
registry and no human handoff cards.

Implemented in `app/src/studio.js` (now 1,488 lines, build succeeds):
- 13-phase data-driven `PHASES`: intake/gap analysis, plan, discover (internet
  + open resources), reverse (closed sources), setup, build, test, check, fix,
  amend, implement, report, loop/decision.
- `FREE_SERVICES` registry mapping paid capabilities to free substitutes, used
  automatically during setup; no purchase required.
- Human gate produces handoff cards with the exact walkthrough, field or
  permission needed and a continue-without fallback; other members keep working.
- Gaps, sources with URLs, attempts and evidence are shown in the UI and written
  into reports; `MAX_REA_ATTEMPTS` and acceptance criteria drive the loop.
- Verification markers: `FREE_SERVICES` 6, handoff 44, gap 36, discover 10,
  reverse 8, setup 11, amend 6, implement 7, acceptance 24.
- `docs/TEAM-BRIEF.md` is the updated source of truth (5, 5b, 5c).
- Builder auto-retry paused in `craft.json`; one builder at a time.

chunks.heading: Recommendations ledger
chunks.text:
## Recommendations ledger
- Added `docs/RECOMMENDATIONS.md` and `recommendations` / `still_needed` facts
  in `data/build-facts.json` so the next agent can query priorities offline.
- P0: logged-in capture evidence, IndexedDB checkpoint/resume, one builder only.
- P1: self-evaluation harness, blackboard panel, Vitest phase-runner tests,
  model fallback registry.
- P2: payment guardrails, source provenance UI, retrospective-driven prompts.
- Still needed from the person: dashboard screenshots/HTML, revoke `gho_hV2Y`,
  8 GB SODIMM, elevated service demotion + driver repair, remote-access decision,

chunks.heading: Linux
chunks.text:
# Linux

Supported. Follows the XDG base directory spec; works on Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora and
Arch with the package names swapped.

chunks.heading: Install
chunks.text:
## Install

```bash
# Prerequisites (Debian/Ubuntu)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y git python3 python3-pip nodejs npm curl

# Ollama
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

# Clone and inspect
git clone https://github.com/jayprophit/hive-mind-rea-template.git ~/hive
cd ~/hive
python3 scripts/doctor.py

# Apply
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --apply --scaffold-vault

# One model to start
ollama pull lfm3:1.7b
```

Fedora: `sudo dnf install -y git python3 nodejs npm`.

chunks.heading: Paths
chunks.text:
## Paths

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| OpenCode config | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/opencode/opencode.json` |
| Hermes home | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/hermes` |
| Stack data | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/hive-mind` |
| Vault | `<repo>/obsidian-vault` |

chunks.heading: Notes
chunks.text:
## Notes

- The full reverse-engineering toolchain is most at home here: `gdb`, `binutils`,
  `tshark`, `rizin`, `rizin`, and `ghidra` are all packaged or one download away.
- `tshark` needs `sudo usermod -aG wireshark $USER` and a re-login to capture without root.
- On a headless box, skip Grafana and read the vault directly; nothing depends on it.

chunks.heading: macOS
chunks.text:
# macOS

Supported. Paths resolve to `~/Library/Application Support`; binaries are looked up
in `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` as well as `PATH`.

chunks.heading: Install
chunks.text:
## Install

```bash
# Prerequisites
xcode-select --install                 # git + compilers
brew install ollama node python@3.12

# Clone and inspect
git clone https://github.com/jayprophit/hive-mind-rea-template.git ~/hive
cd ~/hive
python3 scripts/doctor.py

# Apply
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --apply --scaffold-vault

# One model to start
ollama serve &
ollama pull lfm3:1.7b
```

chunks.heading: Paths
chunks.text:
## Paths

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| OpenCode config | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` |
| Hermes home | `~/Library/Application Support/hermes` |
| Stack data | `~/Library/Application Support/hive-mind` |
| Vault | `<repo>/obsidian-vault` |

chunks.heading: Notes
chunks.text:
## Notes

- Apple silicon runs CPU inference considerably faster than Intel Macs; a 3B model is
  comfortable at 16 GB unified memory.
- Ghidra and JADX need a JDK 21: `brew install --cask temurin@21`.
- No equivalent of the Windows maintenance script is needed; `doctor.py` covers health.

chunks.heading: Windows 10 / 11
chunks.text:
# Windows 10 / 11

Reference platform. Everything in the template has been exercised here.

chunks.heading: Install
chunks.text:
## Install

```powershell
# 1. Prerequisites
winget install --id Git.Git -e
winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e
winget install --id Ollama.Ollama -e

# 2. Clone (never copy a working tree)
git clone https://github.com/jayprophit/hive-mind-rea-template.git C:\hive
cd C:\hive

# 3. Inspect then apply
python scripts\doctor.py
python scripts\bootstrap.py --apply --scaffold-vault

# 4. One model to start
ollama pull lfm3:1.7b
```

chunks.heading: Paths
chunks.text:
## Paths

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| OpenCode config | `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json` |
| OpenCode agents | `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\agents\` |
| Hermes home | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` |
| Stack data | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hive-mind` |
| Vault | `<repo>\obsidian-vault` |

OpenCode uses `~/.config` on Windows too — that is deliberate, so the same config
paths work on every OS.

chunks.heading: Maintenance
chunks.text:
## Maintenance

```powershell
# Elevated. Restore point, WinSxS + WU cache cleanup, DISM/SFC, TRIM,
# page file, power plan, stale driver report.
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\repair-windows-admin.ps1

# Preview without changing anything
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\repair-windows-admin.ps1 -ReportOnly
```

chunks.heading: Windows 10 specifics
chunks.text:
## Windows 10 specifics

- PowerShell 5.1 is the default. Both Python scripts avoid PS-only syntax on purpose.
- `winget` may need the App Installer update from the Store first.
- Virtual terminal colours are off on older builds; `doctor.py` degrades to plain text.
- Windows Defender and a third-party AV both running will cost you ~1 GB of RAM.
  Pick one.

chunks.heading: WSL2
chunks.text:
## WSL2

The reverse-engineering tools that behave badly on native Windows live here:

```bash
wsl --install -d Ubuntu
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y gdb binutils tshark
```

Keep the repo on the Windows filesystem and run `doctor.py` from Windows; run the
Linux tooling inside WSL against the same files.

chunks.heading: Hive Mind REA Template
chunks.text:
# Hive Mind REA Template

**A local-first AI development and reverse-engineering suite that runs on any desktop OS.**

Windows 10/11 · macOS · Linux · WSL — one configuration, one vault, one command.

[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-working-brightgreen)](#verified-status)
[![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-blue)](#platform-support)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-see%20LICENSE-lightgrey)](#)

---

chunks.heading: What this is
chunks.text:
## What this is

A reproducible setup for a **local AI team** that does real work on a normal laptop:
it codes, reviews, researches, drives the desktop, reverse-engineers binaries, and
keeps a written record of every turn in an Obsidian vault.

Nothing here needs a cloud API key. Everything degrades gracefully: run one model on
8 GB of RAM, or ten on 32 GB.

**This repo is configuration, not a running system.** It installs *into* a machine.
Runtime state (databases, locks, logs, session history) is deliberately excluded, so
the same checkout works on your Windows 11 laptop, your Windows 10 desktop, a Mac and
a Linux box without carrying stale state between them.

---

chunks.heading: Platform support
chunks.text:
## Platform support

| Platform | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows 11** | Verified working | Reference build. i3-1005G1, 8 GB, Intel UHD. |
| **Windows 10** | Supported | Same scripts. `scripts/doctor.py` handles PowerShell 5.1. |
| **WSL2 (Ubuntu)** | Supported | Best option for the reverse-engineering toolchain. |
| **macOS** (Intel / Apple silicon) | Supported | Paths resolve to `~/Library/Application Support`. |
| **Linux** (Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora) | Supported | XDG paths. `apt`/`dnf` hints in `core/stack.yaml`. |

The installers are written but only the Windows path has been exercised end to end.
Treat macOS/Linux as *expected to work, not yet proven* — run `scripts/doctor.py`
and open an issue with its output if something is off.

---

chunks.heading: Quick start
chunks.text:
## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jayprophit/hive-mind-rea-template.git
cd hive-mind-rea-template
python scripts/doctor.py          # what does this machine already have?
python scripts/bootstrap.py       # dry run: show what would change
python scripts/bootstrap.py --apply --scaffold-vault
```

Then pull one small model and start:

```bash
ollama pull lfm3:1.7b             # 1.1 GB, tool calling, fast on CPU
ollama serve
```

Windows users get a one-file maintenance script as well:

```powershell
# In an *Administrator* PowerShell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\repair-windows-admin.ps1
```

---

chunks.heading: How it is organised
chunks.text:
## How it is organised

```
core/
  stack.yaml            Single source of truth: components, ports, models, roles.
                        Nothing OS-specific lives here.
scripts/
  doctor.py             Cross-platform health check. No dependencies.
  bootstrap.py          Cross-platform installer and config writer.
platforms/              Per-OS notes and shims.
  windows/  macos/  linux/
opencode/
  agents/*.md           22 agent prompts, portable markdown.
hermes/
  profiles/             Role configs. State files are git-ignored.
obsidian-vault/         The second brain. Exactly one vault.
grafana/provisioning/   Datasources + work-matrix dashboard.
docker/                 Optional heavy services (OpenProject, Chatwoot, LiveKit).
docs/                   Architecture, integrations, install notes.
tools/                  Windows maintenance and installer scripts.
```

chunks.heading: The one rule that makes this portable
chunks.text:
### The one rule that makes this portable

> **Config lives in the repo. State lives on the machine.**

`state.db`, `*.lock`, `logs/`, `cache/`, `sessions/`, `*.db-wal` are all git-ignored.
If you ever see a lock file in a commit, that is a bug — it will be inherited by the
next machine and wedge it.

---

chunks.heading: The stack
chunks.text:
## The stack

| Layer | Component | Port | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Models | **Ollama** | 11434 | Local LLM runtime |
| Supervisor | **Hermes** | CLI | Routes work, delegates to roles |
| Coding | **OpenCode** | CLI | Subagents, structured edits, MCP |
| Investigation | **Craft Anything** | stdio/MCP | How does this software actually work |
| Desktop control | **OpenClaw** | 18789 | Files, Office, browser, screen |
| Dashboards | **Grafana** | 3000 | Work matrix over the vault |
| Knowledge | **Obsidian** | vault | The second brain |
| Optional | **Docker** | 2375 | Heavy services, start only when needed |

chunks.heading: Reverse-engineering toolchain
chunks.text:
### Reverse-engineering toolchain

`Craft Anything` (MCP) · `Ghidra` · `JADX` · `Rizin` · `mitmproxy` · `Frida`
· `tshark` · `GDB` · `objdump` · `ffmpeg` · `yt-dlp`

On Windows, the ELF/GDB/packet tools are best run inside **WSL2** rather than
natively. `scripts/doctor.py` reports which are present.

---

chunks.heading: Research and reporting toolkit
chunks.text:
## Research and reporting toolkit

Four dependency-free scripts turn "find something out" into a document you can
hand to someone. They exist because hosted search billed per query and stopped
working when the balance ran out, while a script that scrapes Google or Bing
gets a bot challenge instead of results.

| Script | Does | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/research.py` | Search, fetch pages as readable text | nothing |
| `scripts/office.py` | Write `.xlsx` `.docx` `.pptx` `.csv` | `pip install openpyxl python-docx python-pptx` |
| `scripts/viz.py` | Charts (SVG/HTML) and Mermaid diagrams | nothing |
| `scripts/doctor.py` | Health check | nothing |

```bash
python -m pip install --user openpyxl python-docx python-pptx

python scripts/research.py "ideapad 3 15iil05 memory upgrade"
python scripts/research.py --url https://download.lenovo.com/consumer/mobiles/emcn60ww.txt
python scripts/research.py --hn "opencode mcp server"

python scripts/viz.py --from samples/ram-options.json --chart bar \
    --x Module --y Price_GBP -o ram.svg --title "RAM options" --html

python scripts/office.py --from samples/ram-options.json --to xlsx ram.xlsx
python scripts/office.py --from samples/ram-options.json --to docx ram.docx
python scripts/office.py --from samples/ram-options.json --to pptx ram.pptx
```

chunks.heading: One file, every office suite
chunks.text:
### One file, every office suite

`.docx`, `.xlsx` and `.pptx` are ZIP-based Open XML. Microsoft Office, Google
Workspace, LibreOffice, OnlyOffice and WPS all read them, and Google Drive
converts them on upload. For a native Google file, upload the Microsoft one and
let Drive convert, or hand over the `.csv` for Sheets.

Charts are SVG — vector, so they stay sharp at any zoom, and they open in a
browser, Word, PowerPoint, LibreOffice and Google Slides. Diagrams are Mermaid
source, rendered by GitHub, GitLab, Obsidian, VS Code and the OpenCode Review
pane, so they stay editable as text instead of becoming a picture.

chunks.heading: Why not use a search API
chunks.text:
### Why not use a search API

A key works and is the right answer if you have one — Brave (2,000/month free)
and Tavily (1,000/month) both have free tiers. Without one, this toolkit uses
endpoints that answer plain HTTP: Marginalia, Hacker News (Algolia), Wikipedia,
and direct page fetch. Verified on 2026-11-19: Google required JavaScript,
Bing returned unrelated results, DuckDuckGo served a bot challenge, and no
public SearXNG instance answered. The browser reaches all of them, because a
real browser passes the checks a script cannot.

---

chunks.heading: Second brain
chunks.text:
## Second brain

One vault. **Exactly one.**

```
obsidian-vault/
  Daily/            one note per day, one row per agent turn
  Work/             PROJECT_MATRIX.md — the master tracker
  Projects/         one note per project
  Templates/        Daily.md, Project.md
  Dashboards/       saved queries, Grafana links
```

Every agent turn writes **one row**, keyed by `requestId`. Replaying the same request
updates the row instead of appending a duplicate. That single constraint is what keeps
the vault readable after a thousand turns.

chunks.heading: About `graphify` and `demobase`
chunks.text:
### About `graphify` and `demobase`

These are listed in `core/stack.yaml` as **optional index layers, disabled by default**:

- `graphify` — a graph export of wikilinks (Obsidian already draws this natively).
- `demobase` — a sample/vector store for demos.

Neither ships with this template and neither exists on the reference machine. If you
want a semantic layer over the vault, pick **one** and point it at `obsidian-vault/`.
Do not let two tools both write an index into the same vault.

For an index that **does** ship and works offline today, use `data/knowledge.db`
(SQLite + FTS5). It is built from the vault, docs and build facts — no graph engine,
no extra service — and is regenerated by `scripts/build_index.py`.

---

chunks.heading: Knowledge base (pull this first)
chunks.text:
## Knowledge base (pull this first)

`data/` is a self-contained, offline index of the repo plus the verified build
facts. It is committed, so a fresh clone on the desktop has it immediately.

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `data/build-facts.json` | machine, toolchain, MCP, projects, lessons, pending work |
| `data/knowledge.db` | SQLite + FTS5; any language or DB browser can read it |
| `data/index.json` | structured dump for diffs and non-SQL tools |
| `scripts/build_index.py` | rebuild both after editing docs |
| `scripts/query.py` | search and read from the terminal |

```bash
python scripts/query.py --stats
python scripts/query.py --search "bios ram"
python scripts/query.py --facts machine
python scripts/query.py --facts pending
python scripts/query.py --doc docs/MCP-WIRING.md
```

On the desktop, the same commands work after `git clone`; nothing needs a
network connection or an API key. See `data/README.md` for the schema.

Prioritised next steps and the outstanding asks are in
[`docs/RECOMMENDATIONS.md`](docs/RECOMMENDATIONS.md) and queryable with
`python scripts/query.py --facts recommendations`.

Deep research into Claude Code's skills/subagents/hooks/workflows/agent-teams,
plus the free reverse-engineered ecosystems (Grok Bot, Manus, Codex, Hermes,
OpenClaw) and general REA practice, is in
[`docs/CLAUDE-CODE-DEEP-DIVE.md`](docs/CLAUDE-CODE-DEEP-DIVE.md).

---

chunks.heading: REA loop
chunks.text:
## REA loop

```
Plan → Design → Build → Check → Research → Recheck → Build → Fix → Amend
  → Compare → Feedback → Fine-tune → Plan → Build → Discovery → Test
  → Compare → Gather data → Weakness/Gaps → Improve → Next version
```

Each pass ends with a written row in `Daily/` and `Work/PROJECT_MATRIX.md`.
The vault is the memory; the loop is the thing that keeps it honest.

---

chunks.heading: Moving to a Windows 10 desktop
chunks.text:
## Moving to a Windows 10 desktop

1. **Install prerequisites** on the desktop: Git, Python 3.10+, Node LTS, Ollama.
   ```powershell
   winget install --id Git.Git -e
   winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e
   winget install --id Ollama.Ollama -e
   ```
2. **Clone, don't copy.** Copying a working tree brings stale locks with it.
   ```powershell
   git clone https://github.com/jayprophit/hive-mind-rea-template.git C:\hive
   cd C:\hive
   ```
3. **Check the machine before changing it.**
   ```powershell
   python scripts\doctor.py
   ```
4. **Apply config.**
   ```powershell
   python scripts\bootstrap.py --apply --scaffold-vault
   ```
5. **Pull one model only** until you know the RAM headroom.
   ```powershell
   ollama pull lfm3:1.7b
   ```
6. **Run the maintenance script** once, elevated, to clear caches and check drivers.
7. **Merge your notes.** Copy only `.md` files from the old vault — never `.obsidian/`
   workspace state, which is per-machine.
8. **Wire Craft Anything to every agent, then prove it works.**
   ```powershell
   .\tools\wire-craft-anything.ps1 -Agent opencode,hermes
   .\tools\agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider
   ```
   Do this before the first build. It catches a stopped Ollama, a missing MCP entry,
   or a model that returns empty content — the three causes of a silent 15-minute run.
   Details: `docs/MCP-WIRING.md`.

Windows 10 differences that

chunks.heading: Moving to a Windows 10 desktop
chunks.text:
Ollama, a missing MCP entry,
   or a model that returns empty content — the three causes of a silent 15-minute run.
   Details: `docs/MCP-WIRING.md`.

Windows 10 differences that matter:

- PowerShell 5.1 is the default shell. `scripts/doctor.py` and `bootstrap.py` avoid
  PowerShell-only syntax, so they behave the same there.
- `winget` may need the App Installer update from the Store before it works.
- Windows 10 has no `SetConsoleMode` VT by default in older builds; `doctor.py`
  falls back to plain text automatically.

---

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting
chunks.text: ## Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: "The agent stops mid-prompt and never finishes"
chunks.text:
### "The agent stops mid-prompt and never finishes"

Check the provider balance, not the MCP server. In the reference build this was
`AI.Error: Insufficient balance` from the hosted provider — the local stack was fine.
Run `python scripts/doctor.py`; if every local check passes, the failure is upstream.
Point the agent at a local model to confirm:

```bash
opencode --model ollama/lfm3:1.7b
```

chunks.heading: A `rea` MCP server closes immediately
chunks.text:
### A `rea` MCP server closes immediately

Corrupted `npx` cache — the module graph is incomplete. Symptom:

```
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find module '@jridgewell/trace-mapping'
```

Fix:

```bash
rm -rf ~/AppData/Local/npm-cache/_npx/*   # Windows
rm -rf ~/.npm/_npx/*                      # macOS / Linux
npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 --version         # verify, then restart Hermes
```

`rea` also needs `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` set to a Python with `pwntools` installed.

chunks.heading: `pip` fails with `No module named 'pip._vendor...'`
chunks.text:
### `pip` fails with `No module named 'pip._vendor...'`

A corrupted pip install. Repair in place:

```bash
python -m ensurepip --upgrade
python -m pip install --user pwntools
```

chunks.heading: Craft Anything says "not installed" but it is
chunks.text:
### Craft Anything says "not installed" but it is

GUI installers do not add themselves to `PATH`. `doctor.py` and `bootstrap.py` probe
the conventional install roots (`C:\Program Files\Craft Anything`,
`/Applications/Craft Anything.app/Contents/MacOS`, `~/.local/bin`) before giving up.

chunks.heading: Hermes: `Failed to load plugin 'obsidian-memory': No __init__.py`
chunks.text:
### Hermes: `Failed to load plugin 'obsidian-memory': No __init__.py`

v3 of that plugin is dashboard-only. The loader expects an importable package.
Add a one-line `__init__.py` in the plugin directory, or disable the plugin — the
dashboard mounts from `dashboard/api.py` regardless.

chunks.heading: Craft Anything or Hermes sits for 15 minutes with no output
chunks.text:
### Craft Anything or Hermes sits for 15 minutes with no output

That is a dead run, not slow work. It has three usual causes, in this order:

1. **The model provider is down.** Hermes' `provider: custom` points at
   `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`; if Ollama was stopped to save RAM, every call
   times out three times and Hermes exits `2`.
2. **The model cannot act.** A model with no chat template (e.g. `bonsai-2:4b`,
   `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}`) burns hidden tokens and returns empty content.
   Measured here: 57.7 s and ~200 tokens to answer "OK".
3. **Two runs collide.** Craft Anything retries every ~90 s; a manual
   `hermes -z ...` at the same time produces `Gateway disconnected`.

Run the preflight before the build, and only one builder at a time:

```powershell
.\tools\agent-preflight.ps1 -StartProvider
```

It tests the MCP handshake (38 tools), the OpenCode and Hermes entries, the
provider, and a real model reply. Full diagnosis: `docs/MCP-WIRING.md`.

---

chunks.heading: Verified status
chunks.text:
## Verified status

Measured on the reference machine (Windows 11 26200, i3-1005G1, 8 GB, WD SN550 250 GB):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/doctor.py` | 20 pass, 6 warn, 0 fail |
| `tools/agent-preflight.ps1` | 7/7 PASS (MCP, OpenCode, Hermes, provider, model) |
| Craft Anything MCP handshake | OK — `craft-anything 0.6.0`, **38 tools** over stdio |
| Hermes MCP test | Connected in 3.9 s, 38 tools |
| Hermes model | `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free` via Nous (free), tool calls OK, 9k prompt in 2.6 s |
| OpenCode model | `opencode/hy4-flash-free` (free), "OK" in 2.7 s |
| Craft Anything builder | OpenCode, free model; build progressing |
| `rea-agents@6.7.0` MCP handshake | OK — `rea 6.7.0` |
| Ollama | 0.40.16, 3 models, listening on :11434 |
| Grafana | responding on :3000 |
| SSD | WD Blue SN550, healthy |
| BIOS | `EMCN60WW` (2024-12-04), updated from `EMCN42WW` |
| `data/knowledge.db` | 107 documents, 388 chunks, 123 facts |

Known warnings on that machine, all expected: 7.7 GB usable RAM, ~21 GB free disk,
Docker daemon stopped, `opencode` CLI not on `PATH`, three Obsidian vault copies.

---

chunks.heading: Requirements
chunks.text:
## Requirements

| | Minimum | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| RAM | 8 GB | 16 GB |
| Disk | 20 GB free | 60 GB free |
| CPU | 2 cores, AVX2 | 4 cores |
| GPU | none (CPU inference) | 6 GB+ VRAM |

At 8 GB, run **one** model at a time (1.5B–4B parameters). Close browsers before
starting an agent session. This is the single biggest performance factor, larger than
any driver update.

platform, resolves per-OS paths, and writes declarative config that each host

    python scripts/bootstrap.py --apply         # write configs
    python scripts/bootstrap.py --apply --install

------------
1. Nothing is written outside the OS-conventional config/data dirs unless asked.
2. Every write is idempotent and merged, never a blind overwrite.
